summary: Blueprint of the new roadmap PurityForFlatCohomology after Česnavičius–Scholze, Purity for flat cohomology (Ann. of Math. 199 (2024)), and Česnavičius, Purity for the Brauer group (Duke 2019), at target level: 57 nodes in seven layers. PF.0 sets up the punctured spectrum, fppf cohomology with supports with its local-to-global spectral sequence, the regular-sequence vanishing and the non-Noetherian Hartogs lemma. PF.1 defines the virtual dimension and proves the étale-depth bound (Theorem 3.2.4) and Zariski–Nagata purity for vdim ≥ 3 (Theorem 3.3.1). PF.2 proves purity in characteristic p through the root-extraction lemma 4.1.11 and the finite-cover lemma 4.1.12. PF.3 develops the Dieudonné side, arc descent of both sides and the analysis over products of perfectoid valuation rings, giving the key formula (Theorem 6.1.1) and purity for perfectoid rings (Theorem 6.1.2). PF.4 proves the main theorems 6.2.3, 6.2.4 and 6.2.7; PF.5 the global consequences, Moret-Bailly's purity for torsors, Gabber's conjectures 2 and 3 and purity for groups of multiplicative type; PF.6 Česnavičius's purity for the Brauer group and for tori, the Auslander–Goldman intersection formula and the residue sequences. Absolute purity, Zariski–Nagata purity for regular rings, local Grothendieck–Lefschetz, complete intersections and the scheme and Brauer foundations are imported from TauCetiRoadmap; arc descent, perfectoid algebra and prismatic Dieudonné modules from atlas supplier packets (PD.6 targets checked individually; its whole packet remains needs_changes). Flat cohomology over animated rings (CS24 §§4.1, 5), the integral-valuation and explicit-tilt refinements and the local Lefschetz theorem 3.2.3 are recorded gaps owned by the pending Part II designs of SchemeAndStackFoundations, PerfectoidQuotients and EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves. The regular towers of CS24 Lemma 3.1.1 are imported from the existing PerfectoidSpaces P7 targets.

nodes.title: The punctured spectrum of a semilocal ring
nodes.statement: For a semilocal commutative ring R (finitely many maximal ideals), the punctured spectrum U_R is the open subscheme of Spec R obtained by removing all closed points: U_R = Spec R ∖ V(J), where J is the Jacobson radical of R. For a local ring (R, 𝔪) this is Spec R ∖ {𝔪}. When R is Noetherian, U_R is quasi-compact; for nonzero R it is empty exactly when R has Krull dimension 0. For the zero ring it is empty as well, but Mathlib assigns that ring dimension ⊥.
hypotheses: R a commutative semilocal ring; quasi-compactness of U_R is asserted only when R is Noetherian, or more generally when J is the radical of a finitely generated ideal.
The closed points removed are all maximal ideals, so for a nonlocal semilocal ring U_R is not the complement of one point.

Ownership: LocalPurity §1.1 already owns IsLocalRing.puncturedSpectrum and its local basic-open/compactness API. This target adds the semilocal adapter and the finite-map/completion compatibilities; it imports the local carrier through the SF.0 supplier contract.
proofSteps: Reuse LocalPurity §1.1 for local R. Extend to semilocal R by taking the complement of V(J), where J is the Jacobson radical; this removes all and only the finitely many maximal ideals. The local compatibility map identifies this open with the imported local punctured spectrum.
For R Noetherian, J is finitely generated, so Spec R ∖ V(J) is a finite union of principal opens D(f_i) and is quasi-compact.
For nonzero semilocal R, U_R is empty iff every prime is maximal, equivalently ringKrullDim R = 0. Treat the zero ring separately: its spectrum is empty and its dimension is ⊥.

sources.match: The punctured spectrum of a semilocal ring is defined there as the complement of all closed points; in the local case it is the complement of the maximal ideal.

U_R = Spec(R) ∖ {𝔪} for Noetherian local R is the open on which the statements about local Picard groups, local Brauer groups and finite étale covers are phrased; the flat purity theorems themselves are phrased through H^i_𝔪(R, G).

nodes.title: Flat cohomology with supports and its local-to-global spectral sequence
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme, Z ⊂ X a closed subset with open complement j : U = X ∖ Z → X, and F an abelian sheaf on the big fppf site of X (for instance a commutative group scheme over X, finite locally free or smooth or of multiplicative type, or the sheaf 𝒢^a attached to a quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-module 𝒢). Define RΓ_Z(X, F) as the fibre of restriction RΓ_fppf(X, F) → RΓ_fppf(U, F) and H^i_Z(X, F) as its cohomology; equivalently H^i_Z(X, −) are the right derived functors of Γ_Z(X, F) = ker(F(X) → F(U)) on fppf abelian sheaves. Writing ℋ^j_Z(−, F) for the étale sheafification of X' ↦ H^j_{Z×_X X'}(X', F) on X_ét, there is a spectral sequence E_2^{ij} = H^i_ét(X, ℋ^j_Z(−, F)) ⇒ H^{i+j}_Z(X, F). When U → X is quasi-compact and F is a finitely presented commutative group scheme (or 𝒢^a with 𝒢 quasi-coherent), the stalk of ℋ^j_Z(−, F) at a geometric point x̄ is H^j_{Z_x̄}(Spec 𝒪^sh_{X,x̄}, F) with Z_x̄ = Z ×_X Spec 𝒪^sh_{X,x̄}.
hypotheses: X any scheme; Z closed; F an abelian fppf sheaf on the big fppf site of X (Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fppfTopology restricted to schemes over X).
The stalk formula for ℋ^j_Z requires U → X quasi-compact and F locally of finite presentation; without quasi-compactness only the colimit over étale neighbourhoods is asserted.

Ownership: SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.7 supplies the derived-support formalism. This target specializes it to the big fppf site and adds the étale local-to-global/stalk comparison, descent and continuity interfaces used here.
proofSteps: Define RΓ_Z as the fibre of restriction, using SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.1–2.2 for cohomology on sites and pullback along U → X; Γ_Z is left exact and injective fppf sheaves restrict to injectives on U, which identifies the fibre with the derived functors of Γ_Z.

The long exact sequence of the pair, excision (H^i_Z(X, F) ≅ H^i_Z(V, F) for an open V ⊃ Z, and H^i_Z(X, F) ≅ H^i_{Z'}(X', F) for an étale X' → X inducing Z' = Z ×_X X' ≅ Z) and the triple sequence for Z' ⊂ Z follow from the fibre description and from the Čech sequence for the fppf (in fact étale) covering {U, X'} of X (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.2).

The local-to-global spectral sequence is the Leray spectral sequence of the composite of RΓ_ét(X, −) with the étale-sheafified local functor RℋZ; this is SGA 4 V 6.4 in the étale case and Bouthier–Česnavičius, Lemma 2.3.2 in the fppf case, cited in CS24 Lemma 7.1.1.

The stalk formula follows by writing Spec 𝒪^sh_{X,x̄} as the limit of affine étale neighbourhoods and using that fppf cohomology of a finitely presented group commutes with such limits on quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes; quasi-compactness of U → X makes U ×_X Spec 𝒪^sh_{X,x̄} the limit of the U ×_X X'.

For smooth commutative G and for quasi-coherent 𝒢 the comparisons with étale and with Zariski cohomology with supports follow from SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.10 (smoothGroup_fppf_etale_comparison, quasiCoherent_topology_comparison) and the five lemma.

For nested supports, use ℋ_Z ℋ_W = ℋ_Z on injectives and preservation of injective/acyclic objects by the sheaf-support functor. This is the support localization formalism of SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.7, specialized to the chosen site; it does not identify non-Noetherian geometric supports with the native colimit-of-Ext module functor.

nodes.title: Regular sequences force vanishing of cohomology with supports
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, M an A-module, Z ⊂ Spec A a closed subset and a_1, …, a_d ∈ A a weakly M-regular sequence each of whose members vanishes on Z. Then H^i_Z(Spec A, M~) = 0 for i < d. Consequently, if M admits a resolution 0 → P_1 → P_0 → M → 0 by A-modules P_k for which a_1, …, a_{d+1} is weakly regular (for instance P_k finite projective and a_1, …, a_{d+1} weakly A-regular vanishing on Z), then H^i_Z(Spec A, M~) = 0 for i < d.
hypotheses: No Noetherian hypothesis: A arbitrary, M arbitrary; weakly regular means each a_k is a nonzerodivisor on M/(a_1, …, a_{k−1})M, with no nonvanishing condition on the last quotient (EGA convention used by CS24 §1.4).
Cohomology with supports is Zariski cohomology of M~, equal to fppf cohomology with supports of the associated sheaf by PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports.
proofSteps: Put W = V(a_1, …, a_d), so Z ⊂ W. The finite principal-open cover of Spec A ∖ W computes supported cohomology by the augmented Čech complex, equivalently the filtered colimit of the Koszul cochain complexes for (a_1^n, …, a_d^n). Powers remain weakly M-regular, so these complexes have zero cohomology below degree d. This argument localizes on Spec A and gives ℋ^j_W(M~) = 0 for j < d.

Use the nested-support identity Rℋ_Z Rℋ_W(M~) ≅ Rℋ_Z(M~) from PF.0. Left t-exactness gives the same lower bound for Z, even when Spec A ∖ Z is not quasi-compact. Taking derived global sections preserves this bound. No commutation of localization with cohomology on a non-qc complement is assumed.
For 0 → P_1 → P_0 → M → 0, use the support long exact sequence and vanishing for P_0 and P_1 below d + 1. Then both H^i_Z(P_0) and H^{i+1}_Z(P_1) vanish when i < d.

The hypothesis that the a_k vanish on Z cannot be dropped: for Z = Spec A and d ≥ 1, H^0_Z(A) = A ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Hartogs extension along closed subsets of large regular depth
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme and Z ⊂ X a closed subset. (a) If for every z ∈ Z the maximal ideal 𝔪_{X,z} contains an 𝒪_{X,z}-regular element, then Y(X) → Y(X ∖ Z) is injective for every separated X-scheme Y. (b) If for every z ∈ Z the maximal ideal 𝔪_{X,z} contains an 𝒪_{X,z}-regular sequence of length 2, then Y(X) → Y(X ∖ Z) is bijective for every X-affine X-scheme Y; in particular Γ(X, 𝒪_X) → Γ(X ∖ Z, 𝒪_X) is bijective.
hypotheses: X arbitrary (not necessarily Noetherian or locally Noetherian); for Noetherian local rings the hypotheses say depth ≥ 1, respectively ≥ 2, at every point of Z.
Y separated in (a); Y affine over X in (b).
proofSteps: (a) The diagonal of Y is a closed immersion, so it suffices that no nonzero local section f of 𝒪_X vanishes off Z: if f vanished on a maximal open U ⊋ X ∖ Z with U ≠ X, take a generic point z of X ∖ U and an 𝒪_{X,z}-regular m ∈ 𝔪_{X,z}; then 𝒪_{X,z} → 𝒪_{X,z}[1/m] is injective and f dies in the target, a contradiction.

(b) Injectivity is (a). Working locally, embed Y into an affine space over X and reduce to Y = 𝔸^1_X, i.e. to extending functions. Take the largest open U ⊃ X ∖ Z to which a given function extends; at a generic point z of X ∖ U a limit argument reduces to bijectivity of 𝒪_{X,z} → Γ(Spec 𝒪_{X,z} ∖ {z}, 𝒪).

For Noetherian 𝒪_{X,z} this is EGA IV 5.10.5 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.6, coherent_hartogs). In general, for an 𝒪_{X,z}-regular pair m_1, m_2, the Čech complex 𝒪 → 𝒪[1/m_1] ⊕ 𝒪[1/m_2] → 𝒪[1/(m_1m_2)] is the filtered colimit of the Koszul complexes K(m_1^n, m_2^n) (Stacks 0913), whose first homology vanishes because m_1^n, m_2^n is again regular (Stacks 07DV).

sources.match: Injectivity for separated targets under a regular element at each point of Z, and bijectivity for X-affine targets under a regular sequence of length two, proved through the Koszul description of the Čech complex of two localizations.

nodes.title: The virtual dimension of a Noetherian local ring
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be a Noetherian local ring with residue field k. By the Cohen structure theorem the 𝔪-adic completion is R̂ ≅ R̃/I for a complete regular local ring R̃ and an ideal I. The virtual dimension is vdim(R) = dim(R̃) − μ(I) ∈ ℤ, where μ(I) = dim_k(I ⊗_{R̃} k) is the minimal number of generators of I. It does not depend on the presentation (SGA 2 XIV 5.2), and for any surjection B → R̂ from a regular local ring B with kernel J, vdim(R) = dim B − μ(J). Grothendieck calls this number the geometric depth of R.
hypotheses: R Noetherian local; vdim takes values in ℤ and may be negative.
μ(I) is the minimal number of generators, Mathlib's Submodule.spanFinrank of I; dimensions are Krull dimensions (ringKrullDim).
proofSteps: Existence of a presentation: Cohen's theorem (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/cohen-structure-and-compatible-coefficients).

Independence (SGA 2 XIV 5.2): if B → B' → R̂ is a factorisation through surjections of regular local rings with J = ker(B → B'), then J is generated by part of a regular system of parameters, dim B' = dim B − μ(J), and 0 → J ⊗ k → I ⊗ k → I' ⊗ k → 0 is exact; two arbitrary presentations are dominated by a third, a power series ring over a Cohen ring mapping onto both.

Comparison with dim: dim R̂ ≥ dim R̃ − μ(I) by Krull's height theorem, with equality iff a minimal generating set of I is part of a system of parameters of R̃, iff it is a regular sequence (R̃ is Cohen–Macaulay), iff R is a complete intersection (SGA 2 XIV 5.4); being cut out by a regular sequence does not depend on the regular local presentation (Stacks 09Q1; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §3.4, requested from R03.3).

Flat base change with separable residue fibre (SGA 2 XIV 5.5): for a flat local R → R' with R'/𝔪R' a separable field extension of k, a presentation of R̂ lifts to a presentation of R̂' with the same μ, so vdim(R') = vdim(R); this covers the henselization and the strict henselization.

sources.match: The virtual dimension is dim(R̃) minus the minimal number of generators of I for a Cohen presentation of the completion; it is independent of the presentation, bounded by dim R with equality exactly for complete intersections, and invariant under completion, henselization and strict henselization.

sources.match: Independence of dim B − μ(I) from the regular presentation, the definition as geometric depth, the inequality with dim and the complete-intersection case of equality, and invariance under flat local maps whose closed fibre is a separable field extension.

nodes.title: Additivity of the virtual dimension along flat local maps
nodes.statement: For a flat local homomorphism R → R' of Noetherian local rings with maximal ideal 𝔪 of R, vdim(R') = vdim(R) + vdim(R'/𝔪R'). Equivalently, the complete-intersection defect cid = dim − vdim is additive: cid(R') = cid(R) + cid(R'/𝔪R').
hypotheses: R → R' flat and local; R and R' Noetherian; the closed fibre R'/𝔪R' is a Noetherian local ring with its own virtual dimension.
proofSteps: Dimension is additive along flat local maps (EGA IV 6.1.2), so the two formulations are equivalent.

Avramov proves additivity of the complete-intersection defect (Avramov 1977, Proposition 3.6 with equations (3.2.1)–(3.2.2)) through the second deviation of the minimal model of the residue field; this input is recorded as a gap.

Special cases planned without the gap: when the closed fibre is a separable field extension, this is PF.1/virtual-dimension (API virtualDimension_flat_separable); when R and the fibre are complete intersections, R' is a complete intersection by the flat-local criterion of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §3.4, which gives the formula in the form used by CS24 Lemma 4.1.12.

nodes.title: Depth and virtual dimension are incomparable
nodes.statement: (a) A Noetherian local ring R that is Cohen–Macaulay but not a complete intersection has depth_𝔪(R) = dim R > vdim(R). (b) Every regular local ring R̃ of dimension ≥ 3 has an ideal I generated by three elements such that R = R̃/I has depth_𝔪(R) = 0, while vdim(R) ≥ dim R̃ − 3. Hence no inequality between depth and vdim holds in general, and the étale-depth bound of PF.1/etale-depth-virtual-dimension is not a consequence of the depth bound for quasi-coherent coefficients.
hypotheses: R Noetherian local in (a); R̃ regular local in (b).
proofSteps: (a) For Cohen–Macaulay R, depth R = dim R, and dim R > vdim R when R is not a complete intersection (PF.1/virtual-dimension, API virtualDimension_le_dim; SGA 2 XIV 5.4).

(b) By Burch's theorem, in Kohn's form (Kohn 1972, Theorem A), R̃ has a three-generated ideal I with projective dimension pd_{R̃}(R̃/I) = dim R̃; by the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula (PurityOfBranchLocus §0.3, auslander_buchsbaum) depth(R̃/I) = 0. Presenting R = R̃/I with three generators gives vdim(R) ≥ dim R̃ − 3. The existence of such ideals is recorded as a gap (no roadmap plans Burch–Kohn).

sources.match: There is no inequality between depth and vdim: Cohen–Macaulay non-complete-intersections have depth larger than vdim, and three-generated ideals of maximal projective dimension (Burch, Kohn) give depth zero with vdim at least dim R̃ − 3.
vdim ≤ dim with equality exactly for complete intersections.

acceptance: The determinantal ring k⟦x, y, z, w⟧/(xz − y^2, yw − z^2, xw − yz) (the twisted cubic cone) is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension 2, not a complete intersection, with vdim = 4 − 3 = 1 < 2 = depth.
For a complete intersection both depth and vdim equal dim, so (a) is sharp.

nodes.title: The étale depth is at least the virtual dimension (Gabber)
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) and a commutative finite étale R-group G whose order is invertible in R, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < vdim(R).
hypotheses: R Noetherian local, arbitrary otherwise (not necessarily excellent or a complete intersection).
G commutative finite étale over R of order invertible in R; the restriction on the order is removed in PF.4/etale-purity-virtual-dimension.
proofSteps: By the local-to-global spectral sequence of PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports and the invariance vdim(R^sh) = vdim(R) (PF.1/virtual-dimension, SGA 2 XIV 5.5), assume R strictly henselian; then G is constant and a dévissage reduces to G = ℤ/ℓ for a prime ℓ invertible in R.

By the henselian–completion comparison for torsion étale cohomology with supports (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.8/open-henselian-completion, its clause for Noetherian I-henselian rings applied with I = 𝔪 and supports in V(𝔪); CS24 Lemma 3.1.2) assume R complete, R = R̃/(f_1, …, f_n) with R̃ complete regular local and f_1, …, f_n a minimal generating set, so vdim(R) = dim R̃ − n.

Reduction to hypersurfaces (n = 1): for n > 1 put R_1 = R̃/(f_1, …, f_{n−1}), R_2 = R̃/(f_n), R_12 = R̃/(f_1f_n, …, f_{n−1}f_n); set-theoretically Spec R_1 ∩ Spec R_2 = Spec R and Spec R_1 ∪ Spec R_2 = Spec R_12, giving the exact sequence 0 → ℤ/ℓ_{R_12} → ℤ/ℓ_{R_1} ⊕ ℤ/ℓ_{R_2} → ℤ/ℓ_R → 0 of étale sheaves on Spec R̃ (étale sites are insensitive to nilpotents); each R_* has vdim ≥ vdim(R) + 1, so the cohomology-with-supports sequence and induction on n conclude.

Hypersurface case R = R̃/(f): by absolute cohomological purity (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §0.10, Gabber's theorem: Ri^!ℤ/ℓ ≅ ℤ/ℓ(−d)[−2d] at the closed point of the regular R̃ of dimension d) H^i_𝔪(R̃, ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < 2d; the local Lefschetz theorem (CS24 Lemma 3.2.3: H^i_𝔪(R̃, ℤ/ℓ) → H^i_𝔪(R̃/(f), ℤ/ℓ) bijective for i < d − 1) then gives H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) = 0 for i < d − 1 = vdim(R). The local Lefschetz theorem is a recorded gap owned by the pending EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartII design.

The earlier excellent characteristic-zero case of the inequality between étale depth and geometric depth.

For R = k⟦x, y⟧/(xy) (vdim 1) it gives H^0_𝔪(R, ℤ/ℓ) = 0, i.e. no nonzero locally constant function is supported at the closed point.

nodes.title: Zariski–Nagata purity in virtual dimension at least three
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be a Noetherian local ring with punctured spectrum U_R, and let FÉt(R), FÉt(U_R) be the categories of finite étale schemes over Spec R and over U_R. (a) If vdim(R) ≥ 2, pullback FÉt(R) → FÉt(U_R) is fully faithful, U_R is connected and π_1^ét(U_R) → π_1^ét(R) is surjective. (b) If vdim(R) ≥ 3, pullback FÉt(R) → FÉt(U_R) is an equivalence of categories and π_1^ét(U_R) → π_1^ét(R) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: R Noetherian local; no excellence, complete-intersection or normality hypothesis; vdim as in PF.1/virtual-dimension.
Fundamental groups are those of the Galois categories of finite étale covers, with a geometric point of U_R as base point (connectedness of U_R is part of (a)).
proofSteps: Granted full faithfulness, connectedness of U_R follows by comparing sections of Spec R ⊔ Spec R → Spec R and of its restriction to U_R; the statements about π_1 follow from those about the functors by SGA 1 V 6.9–6.10: an exact functor of Galois categories compatible with fibre functors induces a surjection of fundamental groups when it is fully faithful and an isomorphism when it is an equivalence (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0/etale-fundamental-group; requested from IG.0).

Patching along the completion (Ferrand–Raynaud 1970, Proposition 4.2) and flat descent reduce to R complete, R = R̃/(f_1, …, f_n) with R̃ complete regular local and f_1, …, f_n minimal generators of 𝔣 = (f_1, …, f_n).

Let 𝔛 ⊃ 𝔘 be the 𝔣-adic formal completions of Spec R̃ ⊃ U_{R̃}. Étale sites are insensitive to nilpotents, so FÉt(𝔛) ≃ FÉt(R) and FÉt(𝔘) ≃ FÉt(U_R); and FÉt(R̃) ≃ FÉt(𝔛) by the henselian-pair equivalence (Stacks 09ZL; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.14). It remains to study FÉt(R̃) → FÉt(𝔘).

(a) Since vdim(R) = dim R̃ − n ≥ 2, the algebraization of formal sections over punctured spectra (Stacks 0DXR with the cohomological-dimension bound 0DX9) algebraizes a morphism between the 𝔘-restrictions of two finite étale R̃-schemes to a morphism over an open V with U_R ⊂ V ⊂ U_{R̃}, unique up to shrinking V. The complement of V has dimension ≤ n (the f_i cut out its closed point), hence codimension ≥ 2 in Spec R̃, and the morphism extends uniquely by Hartogs (EGA IV 5.10.5; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.6, coherent_hartogs). This gives full faithfulness.

(b) For vdim(R) ≥ 3 the algebraization of coherent formal modules (Stacks 0EJP, with 0DXR for the algebra structure) algebraizes every finite étale 𝔘-scheme to a finite étale scheme over such an open V, now with complement of codimension ≥ 3; Zariski–Nagata purity for the regular ring R̃ (SGA 2 X 3.4(i), planned upstream in LocalPurity §§2.1–2.2: purity for regular local rings of dimension ≥ 2 (Stacks 0BMA) and extension across points where purity holds (Stacks 0EY7)) extends it to a finite étale R̃-scheme. This gives essential surjectivity.

The punctured-spectrum algebraization results (Stacks 0DXR, 0DX9, 0EJP) and the Ferrand–Raynaud patching are recorded as a gap: SchemeAndStackFoundations §§4.7–4.10 states algebraization for proper morphisms and adic thickening systems, not over punctured spectra.

Algebraization of formal sections and of coherent formal modules on punctured spectra of complete Noetherian local rings with dualizing complexes under dimension bounds, the cohomological-dimension bound by the number of generators, and finite étale algebras over henselian pairs.

acceptance: For R regular of dimension 2, vdim = 2, and (a) gives full faithfulness; the equivalence for regular R of dimension 2 is the stronger Zariski–Nagata theorem itself (LocalPurity §2.1).
For R = k⟦x, y⟧/(xy), vdim = 1 and U_R is the disjoint union of two punctured lines, so U_R is disconnected and (a) fails below vdim 2.

For the A_1 singularity R = ℂ⟦u, v, w⟧/(uw − v^2) (a hypersurface, vdim = dim = 2), the quotient map from ℂ⟦x, y⟧ restricts to a connected étale double cover of U_R, so π_1^ét(U_R) = ℤ/2 ≠ π_1^ét(R) = 1: (b) fails at vdim 2.
For the complete intersection R = k⟦x, y, z, w⟧/(xy − zw) of dimension 3 = vdim, every finite étale cover of U_R extends (SGA 2 X 3.4(ii)).

nodes.title: Vanishing of 𝔾_a, α_p and ℤ/p cohomology below the depth
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be a Noetherian local ring. Then H^i_𝔪(R, 𝔾_a) = 0 for i < depth_𝔪(R). If R is an 𝔽_p-algebra, then also H^i_𝔪(R, α_p) = 0 and H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/p) = 0 for i < depth_𝔪(R). In particular, for a complete intersection R these vanish for i < dim R.
hypotheses: R Noetherian local; for α_p and ℤ/p, R of characteristic p; cohomology is fppf cohomology with supports at the closed point (PF.0).
proofSteps: For 𝔾_a = 𝒪^a, H^i_𝔪(R, 𝔾_a) is local cohomology H^i_𝔪(R) (PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports, API quasiCoherent), which vanishes below the depth (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.7, depth_localCohomology_vanishing; SGA 2 III 3.3(iv)).

In characteristic p the Frobenius-kernel sequence 0 → α_p → 𝔾_a → 𝔾_a → 0 (F(x) = x^p, fppf-surjective because F is finite flat) and the Artin–Schreier sequence 0 → ℤ/p → 𝔾_a → 𝔾_a → 0 (x ↦ x^p − x, étale-surjective; SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11) give the long exact sequences of cohomology with supports from which the vanishing of the outer terms in degrees < depth yields that of the middle.
Complete intersections are Cohen–Macaulay (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3/ci-cohen-macaulay), so depth = dim.

sources.match: The cohomological characterisation of depth gives vanishing of 𝔾_a cohomology with supports below the depth, and the Frobenius-kernel and Artin–Schreier sequences transfer it to α_p and ℤ/p; for complete intersections this is a case of the main theorem.
Vanishing of local cohomology below the depth (cited by CS24 Example 4.1.10).

acceptance: For R = 𝔽_p⟦x, y⟧ (depth 2): H^0_𝔪 = H^1_𝔪 = 0 for α_p and ℤ/p.
For R = 𝔽_p⟦x⟧/(x^2) (depth 0): x ∈ α_p(R) is supported at 𝔪 and H^0_𝔪(R, α_p) ≠ 0, so no vanishing is asserted in degree 0.
For R = 𝔽_p⟦x, y, z, t⟧/(x^2, y^2, xz − yt) (CS24 Remark 6.2.6) the element xy ∈ α_p(R) is killed by a power of 𝔪, so H^0_𝔪(R, α_p) ≠ 0; this is consistent with depth_𝔪(R) = 0.

nodes.title: Extracting roots of the equations of a complete intersection
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring, f_1, …, f_m ∈ A an A-regular sequence, B = A/(f_1, …, f_m), and G a commutative B-group scheme that is smooth or finite locally free. Let n_1, …, n_m > 0 and g_1, …, g_m ∈ A with g_i^{n_i} = f_i, and put B' = A/(g_1, …, g_m). For every ideal I ⊂ B containing a B-regular sequence a_1, …, a_d of length d, restriction H^i_I(B, G) → H^i_{IB'}(B', G) is injective for i < d and bijective for i < d − 1.
hypotheses: A arbitrary commutative ring; regular sequences in the EGA sense (no nonvanishing condition on the final quotient), as in CS24 §1.4.
The elements a_j are taken in B and lifted to A where needed; cohomology is fppf cohomology with supports in V(I) (PF.0).
proofSteps: Reduce to G smooth: the Bégueri resolution 0 → G → Res_{G^*/B}(𝔾_m) → Q → 0 of a finite locally free commutative G by smooth affine commutative groups (CS24 (1.4.2); Bégueri 1980, 2.2.1) and the five lemma reduce the finite locally free case to the smooth case (recorded gap SF-PII-deformation).
For all exponents 0 < e_k ≤ n_k, the sequence g_1^{e_1}, …, g_m^{e_m}, a_1, …, a_d is A-regular (Stacks 07DV, powers of a regular sequence; request to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3).

If n_1 > 1, the closed immersion j : Spec A/(g_1^{n_1−1}, f_2, …, f_m) → Spec B is cut out by the square-zero ideal J = g_1^{n_1−1}A/(f_1, …) which is free of rank one over A/(g_1, f_2, …, f_m). Deformation theory for smooth commutative groups (Česnavičius 2015, Lemma B.14) gives the exact sequence 0 → Hom(e^*Ω^1_{G/B}, J) → G → j_*(G|_{Spec A/(g_1^{n_1−1}, f_2, …)}) → 0 of étale sheaves, whose kernel is a finite projective module over A/(g_1, f_2, …, f_m) (recorded gap SF-PII-deformation).

By PF.0/regular-sequence-support-vanishing applied to that finite projective module and the regular sequence a_1, …, a_d, its cohomology with supports in V(I) vanishes in degrees < d; the long exact sequence makes H^i_I for B → A/(g_1^{n_1−1}, f_2, …) injective for i < d and bijective for i < d − 1.
Iterate through g_1^{n_1−2}, …, g_1 and then induct on m.

sources.match: Injectivity below d and bijectivity below d − 1 of the restriction from A/(f_1, …, f_m) to A/(f_1^{1/n_1}, …, f_m^{1/n_m}) for smooth or finite locally free commutative G, through the Bégueri sequence, Stacks 07DV and the deformation-theoretic exact sequence with a free square-zero ideal.
This lemma is where the complete-intersection hypothesis enters: the square-zero ideals between the successive root quotients are free because the f_i form a regular sequence.
f_1, …, f_r is M-regular iff f_1^{e_1}, …, f_r^{e_r} is.

acceptance: For m = 0 (B = A) the statement is the identity.
In PF.2/char-p-complete-intersection-purity it is applied with A = k⟦t_1^{1/p^∞}, …, t_N^{1/p^∞}⟧ and n_i = p^j, to pass from the equations f_i to their p^j-th roots.

Regularity is what makes J free: for the non-regular pair f_1 = x^2, f_2 = xy in A = k⟦x, y⟧ and g_1 = x, the ideal J = xA/(x^2, xy) ≅ k is killed by y and is not free over A/(x, xy) = k⟦y⟧, so the depth argument breaks down.

nodes.title: Passage to a finite flat cover of complete intersections
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) → (R', 𝔪') be a finite flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings that are complete intersections, let n < dim R be an integer, and let G be a commutative finite flat R-group. Suppose that for every finite nonempty tensor power R' ⊗_R ⋯ ⊗_R R' and every local ring (A, 𝔮) of it at a maximal ideal, H^i_𝔮(A, G) = 0 for i < n. Then H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < n and H^n_𝔪(R, G) → H^n_{𝔪'}(R', G) is injective.
hypotheses: R → R' finite, flat and local; both complete intersections; n < dim R.
proofSteps: Since R and R′ are complete intersections and R→R′ is flat local, its finite-dimensional closed fibre B=R′/𝔪R′ is a complete-intersection algebra over k=R/𝔪 (Stacks 09Q7). Tensor powers B⊗_k⋯⊗_kB and their localizations are complete intersections: use regular-sequence presentations, flat base change and transitivity of local complete-intersection morphisms over a field. Thus every maximal localization A of R′^{⊗(s+1)} is flat local over R with a zero-dimensional complete-intersection closed fibre. The flat-local criterion makes A a complete intersection, and the flat dimension formula gives dim A=dim R. Merely being Artinian would not suffice for the complete-intersection conclusion.
The hypothesis gives H^i_𝔪(R'^{⊗(s+1)}, G) = ⊕_𝔮 H^i_𝔮(A_𝔮, G) = 0 for i < n (excision to the semilocal pieces, PF.0).

The fppf descent spectral sequence E_1^{st} = H^t_𝔪(R'^{⊗(s+1)}, G) ⇒ H^{s+t}_𝔪(R, G) for Spec R' → Spec R (PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports, API finiteFlatDescent) has E_1^{st} = 0 for t < n, which gives the vanishing in degrees < n and the edge injection in degree n.

sources.match: For a finite flat local map of complete intersections, purity in degrees below n on the local rings of all tensor powers implies vanishing below n for R and injectivity in degree n, from the descent spectral sequence for R' over R.
Gabber's spectral-sequence argument for passage to a finite flat cover, which CS24 Lemma 4.1.12 follows.
For a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, the target is a complete intersection iff the source and the closed fibre are.

acceptance: For R' = R it is a tautology.

For R = k⟦t⟧ → R' = k⟦t^{1/p}⟧ (finite flat of degree p, both regular) the tensor powers are k⟦t^{1/p}⟧ ⊗ ⋯, local complete intersections of dimension 1, as used for the passage to perfections in CS24 Proposition 4.1.13.
The complete-intersection hypothesis on R' is needed to apply the hypothesis to the local rings of the tensor powers.

nodes.title: Purity for flat cohomology of complete intersections in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be a complete Noetherian local 𝔽_p-algebra that is a complete intersection with perfect residue field k, and G a commutative finite flat R-group of p-power order. Then H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < dim R.
hypotheses: R complete, local, Noetherian, of characteristic p, a complete intersection, with perfect residue field; G of p-power order.
proofSteps: Induct on i simultaneously for all such R. By the Cohen structure theorem (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/cohen-structure-and-compatible-coefficients) R ≅ k⟦t_1, …, t_N⟧/(f_1, …, f_m) with f_1, …, f_m regular, so dim R = N − m.

PF.2/finite-flat-cover-reduction applied to the finite flat covers k⟦t_1^{1/p^j}, …, t_N^{1/p^j}⟧/(f_1, …, f_m) and a limit argument (PF.0, API limit) reduce to H^i_{(t)}(k⟦t^{1/p^∞}⟧/(f_1, …, f_m), G) = 0 for i < N − m, where k⟦t^{1/p^∞}⟧ is the uncompleted colimit of CS24 (1.4.1).

The ring k⟦t^{1/p^∞}⟧ is perfect, so PF.2/root-extraction-comparison (with the roots f_i^{1/p^j}) and a limit argument reduce to the same vanishing for the perfect ring R_∞ = k⟦t^{1/p^∞}⟧/(f_1^{1/p^∞}, …, f_m^{1/p^∞}).

For the perfect 𝔽_p-algebra R_∞, the positive-characteristic key formula RΓ_Z(R_∞, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(W(R_∞), 𝕄(G))^{V=1} (CS24 Theorem 4.1.8; recorded gap SF-PII-key-formula) and the Dieudonné module 𝕄(G) of projective dimension ≤ 1 over W(R_∞) (PrismaticCohomologyPartII PD.6/perfect-base-classification) reduce to H^i_Z(W(R_∞), W(R_∞)) = 0 for i < N − m + 1 with Z = V(p, t_1, …, t_N).
An R-regular sequence a_1, …, a_{N−m} ⊂ 𝔪 stays R_∞-regular (Stacks 07DV), so p, a_1, …, a_{N−m} is W(R_∞)-regular, and PF.0/regular-sequence-support-vanishing gives the required vanishing.

sources.match: For complete complete-intersection 𝔽_p-algebras with perfect residue field and G of p-power order, H^i_𝔪 vanishes below dim R, by passing to perfect root towers with Lemmas 4.1.11–4.1.12, the key formula (4.1.8.2) and projective dimension ≤ 1 of 𝕄(G).
The positive-characteristic key formula RΓ_Z(S, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(W_n(S), 𝕄(G))^{V=1} for perfect S and G killed by p^n, and the crystalline Dieudonné classification of Berthelot, Gabber and Lau.

acceptance: For R = 𝔽_p⟦x, y⟧ and G = μ_p, H^0_𝔪 = H^1_𝔪 = 0: sections extend uniquely and restriction on H^1 is injective. Surjectivity on H^1 also needs H^2_𝔪 = 0, supplied separately by PF.4/flat-purity-regular.
For G = α_p it recovers PF.2/additive-group-depth-vanishing for complete intersections.

For the non-complete-intersection ring of CS24 Remark 6.2.6 the conclusion fails in degree 0 (PF.4/virtual-dimension-flat-counterexample), so the complete-intersection hypothesis cannot be weakened to vdim.

nodes.title: The Dieudonné side RΓ_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G))^{V=1}
nodes.statement: Let A be a perfectoid ring (integral perfectoid in the sense of PerfectoidQuotients Q0), ξ a generator of ker(θ : A_inf(A) → A), G a commutative finite locally free A-group of p-power order with covariant prismatic Dieudonné module 𝕄(G) (finitely presented, p-power torsion, of projective dimension ≤ 1 over A_inf(A), with Frob-semilinear F and Frob^{-1}-semilinear V, FV = Frob(ξ), VF = ξ), and Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA) closed. Define RΓ_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G))^{V=1} as the fibre of V − 1 : RΓ_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G)) → RΓ_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G)), where Z is viewed as a closed subset of Spec A_inf(A) through A_inf(A) → A → A/p, and V acts on cohomology with supports through its Frob^{-1}-semilinear structure (Frob is an automorphism of A_inf(A) preserving the support). The construction is functorial in A (for a fixed compatible choice of ξ over perfectoid A-algebras), in G and in Z. For a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra and ξ = p it is the complex RΓ_Z(W(A), 𝕄(G))^{V=1} of the crystalline theory.
hypotheses: A perfectoid; the choice of ξ fixes V, and the same ξ is used over all perfectoid A-algebras A' (CS24 §2.1.2 and §4.2.1).
𝕄 is PrismaticCohomologyPartII PD.6/covariant-normalisation's covariant functor; for perfect 𝔽_p-algebras PD.6/perfect-base-classification's crystalline functor.
proofSteps: Cohomology with supports of the A_inf(A)-module 𝕄(G) is Zariski cohomology with supports (PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports, API quasiCoherent); Frob^{-1}-semilinear maps act on it because Frob is a ring automorphism of A_inf(A) fixing V(p, z) for every z vanishing on Z.

Functoriality in A uses that 𝕄 commutes with base change (PD.6/covariant-normalisation), naturality of Fontaine's θ (PerfectoidQuotients Q0/theta-naturality), and that the image of ξ in A_inf(A') is again a distinguished element of ker θ', hence a generator (PrismaticCohomology PR.0/ainf-prism; BMS Lemma 3.10); functoriality in G and Z is that of cohomology with supports.
The comparison with the crystalline case for perfect 𝔽_p-algebras with ξ = p is part of PD.6/covariant-normalisation.

sources.match: The right side of the key formula is the V = 1 part of quasi-coherent cohomology with supports of A_inf(A) with coefficients 𝕄(G), with a fixed ξ defining V; in characteristic p it is the crystalline version with W(S).
𝕄(μ_{p^n}) = A_inf/p^n with F = Frob, V = ξ·Frob^{-1}; 𝕄(ℤ/p^n) = A_inf/p^n with F = Frob(ξ)·Frob, V = Frob^{-1}.

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.PurityForFlatCohomology.dieudonneSide_map
api.statement: Write D(A,G,Z) = RΓ_Z(A_inf(A),𝕄(G))^{V=1}. A perfectoid map A → A′ with compatible ξ and a homomorphism G_{A′} → G′ give D(A,G,Z) → D(A′,G′,Z_{A′}). Separately, for Z′ ⊂ Z_{A′}, extension of supports gives D(A′,G′,Z′) → D(A′,G′,Z_{A′}). Require identity, composition and commuting-square laws; the inclusion of supports points toward the larger support.

api.statement: A short exact sequence 0 → G' → G → G'' → 0 gives a distinguished triangle of Dieudonné sides (exactness of 𝕄, PD.6/covariant-normalisation).

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.PurityForFlatCohomology.dieudonneSide_localization
api.statement: For the open complement U of Z in Spec A_inf(A), there is the natural support triangle RΓ_Z(A_inf,𝕄) → RΓ(A_inf,𝕄) → RΓ(U,𝕄). Compute the last term by the derived limit over the principal-open basis D(z) ⊂ U, including its restriction and intersection maps; apply fib(V − 1) compatibly. This is the indexed localization diagram of CS24 (4.2.7.1), not a product of unrelated localizations.

nodes.title: Low-degree flat cohomology of a perfectoid ring through Dieudonné modules
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid ℤ_p-algebra A and a commutative finite locally free A-group G of p-power order there are identifications G(A) ≅ 𝕄(G)^{V=1} and H^1(A, G) ≅ 𝕄(G)/(V − 1)𝕄(G), functorial in A and G. Moreover H^i(A, G) = 0 for i ≥ 2.
hypotheses: A perfectoid ℤ_p-algebra (integral perfectoid, PerfectoidQuotients Q0); G of p-power order; ξ fixed as in PF.3/dieudonne-side-complex.
proofSteps: For p^n killing G, H^1(A, G) ≅ Ext^1(ℤ/p^n, G) in fppf sheaves of ℤ/p^n-modules, and G(A) = Hom(ℤ/p^n, G).

The exact equivalence G ↦ 𝕄(G) (PD.6/covariant-normalisation) with 𝟙_n := 𝕄(ℤ/p^n) = (A_inf/p^n, F = Frob(ξ)·Frob, V = Frob^{-1}) turns Hom into evaluation at 1, giving G(A) ≅ 𝕄(G)^{V=1}, and turns extensions of 𝟙_n by 𝕄(G) into the classes m ∈ 𝕄(G) modulo (V − 1)𝕄(G): an extension is determined by the value of V on a lift of 1, and isomorphisms change it by V(a) − a (as in CS24 Proposition 4.1.4).
The vanishing for i ≥ 2 is CS24 Remark 4.2.5, deduced in CS24 Corollary 5.3.7 from the perfect case (Corollary 4.1.9) by p-adic continuity; it is recorded in the gap SF-PII-continuity.

sources.match: Over a perfectoid ℤ_p-algebra, G(A) is the V-fixed part of 𝕄(G) and H^1(A, G) is its V − 1 coinvariants, functorially; higher cohomology vanishes by Corollary 5.3.7.
The positive-characteristic prototype with sheaf Hom and Ext of ℤ/p^n-module sheaves.

acceptance: For A perfect of characteristic p and G = ℤ/p it is Artin–Schreier: H^1(A, ℤ/p) = A/(F − 1)A.
For G = μ_p: 𝕄(μ_p)/(V − 1) recovers H^1(A, μ_p) = A^×/A^{×p} by the Kummer sequence (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11).

For A=𝒪_C with C algebraically closed, every finite flat G-torsor has a C-point on its generic fibre. Properness of the finite torsor extends this point to an 𝒪_C-section by the valuative criterion. Hence H^1(𝒪_C,G)=0 for every such G, including those beyond μ_p and ℤ/p.

nodes.title: p-complete arc hyperdescent of the Dieudonné side
nodes.statement: Let A be a perfectoid ℤ_p-algebra, Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA) closed, a ∈ A_inf(A) and G a commutative finite locally free A-group of p-power order. The functors A' ↦ 𝕄(G_{A'})[1/a] and A' ↦ RΓ_Z(A_inf(A'), 𝕄(G_{A'})), on perfectoid A-algebras A', satisfy hyperdescent for p-complete arc hypercovers A' → A'^• whose terms are perfectoid A-algebras; so does the Dieudonné side A' ↦ RΓ_Z(A_inf(A'), 𝕄(G_{A'}))^{V=1}.
hypotheses: Hypercovers in the p-complete arc topology (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.11/AT.12) whose terms are perfectoid; cosimplicial limits are R lim over Δ.
proofSteps: A cosimplicial abelian group computes R lim_Δ by its alternating complex and localisation is exact, so it suffices to treat a = 1.

𝕄(G_{A'}) = 𝕄(G) ⊗_{A_inf(A)} A_inf(A') (PD.6/covariant-normalisation, base change; the tensor product is underived because 𝕄(G) lies in DM_tors, PD.6/torsion-base-change) and 𝕄(G) has a resolution 0 → M_0 → M_1 → 𝕄(G) → 0 by finite projective A_inf(A)-modules which stays exact after base change because 𝕄(G) is p-power torsion and A_inf(A') is p-torsion free (PD.6/torsion-base-change).

A' ↦ A_inf(A') satisfies the required hyperdescent (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.12/integral-perfectoid-hyperdescent, BS22 Proposition 8.10, CS24 Lemma 4.2.6), hence so do A' ↦ M_i ⊗ A_inf(A') and A' ↦ 𝕄(G_{A'}), and also their localisations.

For cohomology with supports, use the triangle RΓ_Z → RΓ → R lim_z RΓ(A_inf(A')[1/z], 𝕄[1/z]) over z ∈ A_inf(A) vanishing on Z, with RΓ(A_inf(A')[1/z], 𝕄[1/z]) = 𝕄(G_{A'})[1/z] on the affine scheme; the fibre of V − 1 commutes with limits.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.2.7 and its proof, pp. 42–43; Lemma 4.2.6, p. 42
sources.match: Hyperdescent of 𝕄(G)[1/a] and of RΓ_Z(A_inf, 𝕄(G)) for p-complete arc hypercovers by perfectoids, from the hyperdescent of A_inf, A and A^♭ (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 8.10) and a two-term projective resolution of 𝕄(G).

nodes.title: Finitely presented modules over a product of rings
nodes.statement: For a family of commutative rings (R_i)_{i∈I} with product R = ∏_i R_i and a finitely presented R-module M, the natural map M → ∏_i (M ⊗_R R_i) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: I an arbitrary index set; M finitely presented (a finite free presentation R^n → R^m → M → 0).
proofSteps: Choose a presentation R^n → R^m → M → 0. The functors − ⊗_R R_i and arbitrary products of abelian groups are right exact, resp. exact, so the claim for M follows from the evident case of finite free modules, R^m = ∏_i R_i^m, by the five lemma.

sources.match: A finitely presented module over a product of rings is the product of its base changes to the factors, by reduction to finite free modules through a presentation.

acceptance: For M = R it is the identity R = ∏ R_i.
Finite presentation is needed: for I infinite and M = ⊕_i R_i (not finitely generated) the map M → ∏_i M ⊗ R_i = ∏_i R_i is not surjective.
For M = R/J with J = ∏ J_i finitely generated, it gives R/J = ∏ R_i/J_i.

nodes.title: Dieudonné modules over a product of perfectoid rings
nodes.statement: For perfectoid rings (A_i)_{i∈I} with product A = ∏_i A_i (perfectoid) and a commutative finite locally free A-group G of p-power order, the natural map 𝕄(G) → ∏_i 𝕄(G_{A_i}) is an isomorphism over A_inf(A) ≅ ∏_i A_inf(A_i), compatibly with F and V when compatible generators ξ of ker θ are used.
hypotheses: A_i perfectoid; the product is perfectoid with tilt ∏ A_i^♭ (PerfectoidQuotients Q0/products-of-perfectoid-rings); ξ = (ξ_i).
proofSteps: W(∏ A_i^♭) = ∏ W(A_i^♭) since Witt vectors are computed componentwise on coordinates.

𝕄(G_{A_i}) = 𝕄(G) ⊗_{A_inf(A)} A_inf(A_i) by base change (PD.6/covariant-normalisation), and 𝕄(G) is finitely presented over A_inf(A), so PF.3/finitely-presented-modules-over-products gives the isomorphism; F and V are compatible because they are compatible with base change.

sources.match: 𝕄(G) over a product of perfectoid rings is the product of the 𝕄(G_{A_i}) over A_inf(A) = ∏ A_inf(A_i), by base change and Lemma 4.2.8.

acceptance: For I a singleton it is the identity.
For G = μ_{p^n}, both sides are ∏ A_inf(A_i)/p^n with V = ξ·Frob^{-1}.

nodes.title: Frobenius-fixed vectors over an algebraically closed field (Katz)
nodes.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and M a finite-dimensional K-vector space with a bijective Frobenius-semilinear map F : M → M (F(am) = a^p F(m)). Then M^{F=1} is a finite-dimensional 𝔽_p-vector space and the natural map M^{F=1} ⊗_{𝔽_p} K → M is an isomorphism compatible with F (acting as 1 ⊗ Frob on the source). Consequently V − 1 is surjective for any bijective Frob^{-1}-semilinear V on M, and ξ·Frob^{-1} − 1 and ξ·x − Frob(x) are surjective on K for ξ ∈ K^×.
hypotheses: K algebraically closed of characteristic p; dim_K M < ∞; F bijective and p-semilinear.
proofSteps: In a basis, F(x) = A x^{(p)} with A invertible. The additive map x ↦ A x^{(p)} − x is finite étale of degree p^n (invertibility of A gives finiteness and the Jacobian is −1). Its kernel therefore has p^n points over algebraically closed K, an 𝔽_p-space of dimension n; this is the field case of Katz Proposition 4.1.1.
Linear independence over K of 𝔽_p-independent F-fixed vectors follows by a minimal-relation argument applying F; comparing dimensions gives the isomorphism.

Apply the fixed-basis result to V^{-1}, which is Frobenius-semilinear. In that basis V − 1 is coordinatewise Frob^{-1} − 1 and is surjective over K. The two scalar variants are likewise surjective because their equations become nonconstant polynomials x^p − c x + b = 0.

sources.match: Over the algebraically closed fraction field of a tilted valuation ring, a finite vector space with bijective F is spanned by its F-fixed points (Katz), which reduces surjectivity of V − 1 to solvability of x^p − ξx + b = 0.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.1.1 and its proof, pp. 142–145 (field case, n = 1)
sources.match: Directly read: unit-root Frobenius modules correspond to finite locally constant ℤ/p^n-modules; over an algebraically closed field the local system is constant and gives a basis of fixed vectors.

acceptance: For M = K with F = Frob, M^{F=1} = 𝔽_p and 𝔽_p ⊗ K = K.
For M = K with F = c·Frob (c ≠ 0), M^{F=1} is spanned by a root of x^{p−1} = c^{-1}, which exists because K is algebraically closed.

Algebraic closedness is needed: for K = 𝔽_3(t)^perf and F = t·Frob, a nonzero fixed vector would give x^2 = 1/t. The t-adic value group of K is ℤ[1/3], which does not contain −1/2, so there is no such vector.

nodes.title: Flat cohomology over products of perfectoid valuation rings
nodes.statement: Let (A_i)_{i∈I} be p-adically complete valuation rings of rank ≤ 1 with algebraically closed fraction fields K_i, A = ∏_i A_i, K = ∏_i K_i, a ∈ A, and G a commutative finite locally free A-group of p-power order. Then: V − 1 is surjective on 𝕄(G)[1/[a^♭]] for any ξ used to define V; H^j(A[1/a], G) = 0 for j ≥ 1; and there is a unique commutative square with top row G(A) ≅ 𝕄(G)^{V=1} (PF.3/perfectoid-low-degree-cohomology), bottom row G(A[1/a]) ≅ (𝕄(G)[1/[a^♭]])^{V=1} and vertical restriction maps, and the vertical maps are bijective when a is a nonzerodivisor. Here a^♭ ∈ A^♭ = ∏ A_i^♭ is a compatible system of p-power roots of a and [−] the Teichmüller lift.
hypotheses: A_i p-adically complete valuation rings of rank ≤ 1 with algebraically closed fraction fields; A is perfectoid (PerfectoidQuotients Q0/products-of-perfectoid-rings).
proofSteps: Each A_i is perfectoid (a p-adically complete rank ≤ 1 valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field: perfect if p = 0, the ring of integers of an algebraically closed perfectoid field otherwise; CS24 (2.1.2.3), recorded in gap PQ-PII-towers), so A is perfectoid with tilt ∏ A_i^♭ (PerfectoidQuotients Q0/products-of-perfectoid-rings). Decompose I into finitely many parts to assume a = 0 or a a nonzerodivisor. Each A_i^♭ is a valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field K_i^♭ (CS24 Proposition 2.1.9, second part; gap PQ-PII-towers), so a^♭ is a nonzerodivisor.

Since A ⊂ A[1/a] ⊂ K and G is finite, G(A) = G(K) by the valuative criterion, so G(A) = G(A[1/a]); the local rings of Spec A[1/a] are valuation rings with fraction fields localizations of K (the connected components of Spec of a product of valuation rings are ultraproduct valuation spectra, ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.11/complete-valuation-product-basis; CS24 Lemma 2.2.4), so every G-torsor over A[1/a] is trivial (valuative criterion locally, K a product of algebraically closed fields) and H^1(A[1/a], G) = 0; the Bégueri resolution (gap SF-PII-deformation) and the absence of nonsplit étale covers give H^j = 0 for j ≥ 2.

Cover Spec A by finitely many opens over which G embeds in an abelian scheme B (Raynaud's embedding, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/raynaud-abelian-embedding, as in BBM 3.1.1); if p^n kills G then G ⊂ B[p^n], a truncated p-divisible group with finite locally free quotient B[p^n]/G. Subdividing I, assume 0 → G → G_1 → G_2 → 0 with G_1 = B[p^n]. By exactness of 𝕄 (PD.6/covariant-normalisation) and the snake lemma reduce to G = B[p^n], and through the filtration by the B[p^i] (whose graded pieces are ≅ B[p]) to G = B[p], the p-torsion of the p-divisible group B[p^∞]; then 𝕄(G) is a finite projective A^♭-module, a direct summand of a finite free one.

Right vertical map: injective as a^♭ is a nonzerodivisor; surjective because a V-fixed m ∈ 𝕄(G)[1/a^♭] with b·m ∈ 𝕄(G) also has b^{1/p}·m ∈ 𝕄(G), and elements b of A^♭[1/a^♭] all of whose p-power roots stay bounded lie in A^♭.

Surjectivity of V − 1: first after base change to ∏ K_i^♭ (Claim 4.2.10.1): factorwise, either A_i has characteristic p and it is (4.2.4.1), or ξ is invertible, F and V are bijective on M = 𝕄(G_{A_i}) ⊗ K_i^♭ and PF.3/frobenius-fixed-points-algebraically-closed applies. Then descend from ∏ K_i^♭ to 𝕄(G)[1/a^♭] stalkwise on Spec A^♭[1/a^♭], whose local rings are perfect valuation rings, using Claim 4.2.10.2: for a perfect valuation ring W with fraction field L, a finite free W-module M and Frob^{-1}-semilinear V, any x ∈ M_L with V(x) − x ∈ M lies in M.
Uniqueness of the square follows from bijectivity of the vertical maps.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.2.10 and its proof with Claims 4.2.10.1–4.2.10.2, pp. 43–45
sources.match: Over products of complete rank-≤1 valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields, V − 1 is surjective on localized Dieudonné modules, flat cohomology of A[1/a] vanishes in positive degrees, and the low-degree identifications are compatible with localization.
Local structure of Spec of a product of valuation rings, and tilting of valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields.

acceptance: For I a singleton and A = 𝒪_C with C algebraically closed perfectoid, a = p: H^j(C, G) = 0 for j ≥ 1 and G(𝒪_C) = G(C).
For G = μ_p: (𝕄(μ_p)[1/[a^♭]])^{V=1} = μ_p(A[1/a]) = μ_p(K) = ∏_i μ_p(K_i), where μ_p(K_i) = ℤ/p if K_i has characteristic 0 and μ_p(K_i) = 0 if it has characteristic p.
The algebraic closedness of the K_i is needed for the surjectivity of V − 1: over a perfectoid field C that is not algebraically closed, H^1(C, ℤ/p) can be nonzero.

nodes.title: p-complete arc hyperdescent of flat cohomology on perfectoids
nodes.statement: For a prime p, a perfectoid ring A, a commutative finite locally free A-group G and a closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA), the functors A' ↦ RΓ(A', G) and A' ↦ RΓ_Z(A', G) satisfy hyperdescent for p-complete arc hypercovers A' → A'^• whose terms are perfectoid A-algebras.
hypotheses: A perfectoid; hypercovers with perfectoid terms; G arbitrary commutative finite locally free (not only of p-power order).
proofSteps: Reduce to Z = Spec(A/p): for a ∈ A vanishing on Z the p-adic completion of A[1/a] is perfectoid (CS24 Corollary 2.1.6; A[1/a] is étale over A, so this is PerfectoidQuotients Q0/completely-etale-and-henselian-perfectoid once derived and classical p-completion agree, which holds by bounded p-torsion), excision (CS24 Theorem 5.4.4 or Corollary 5.3.8; gap SF-PII-excision) gives RΓ_{p=0}(A[1/a], G) ≅ RΓ_{p=0}(A[1/a]^∧, G), and the fibre sequence RΓ_Z(A) → RΓ_{p=0}(A) → R lim_a RΓ_{p=0}(A[1/a]) (5.5.1.1) reduces to supports {p = 0}.

A' ↦ RΓ(A'[1/p], G) satisfies the hyperdescent by arc descent for étale cohomology (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.11/complete-etale-hyperdescent and AT.6/torsion-arc-hyperdescent, CS24 Theorem 2.2.5), so the support triangle reduces to A' ↦ RΓ(A', G).

The prime-to-p part of G is handled by arc descent and Gabber's henselian invariance (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.8/gabber-affine-proper-base-change); for G of p-power order use p-adic continuity RΓ(A', G) ≅ R lim_n RΓ(A'/^L p^n, G) (CS24 Theorem 5.3.5; gap SF-PII-continuity).

A' ↦ A'/^L x satisfies the hyperdescent for x = p and x = π^{1/p^n} (π a unit multiple of p with compatible roots), as the cofibre of multiplication by x on A' ↦ A' (AT.12/integral-perfectoid-hyperdescent); the deformation triangle (CS24 Theorem 5.2.8; gap SF-PII-deformation) reduces from A'/^L p^n to A'/^L p and then, because the fibres of the comparison maps are identified along n, to the filtered colimit A'/^L π^{1/p^∞} ≅ (A'/pA')_red, a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra (CS24 (2.1.2.3) and (2.1.3.2), gap PQ-PII-towers; PerfectoidQuotients Q0/perfectoid-rings-reduced).

For perfect 𝔽_p-algebras the positive-characteristic key formula (CS24 (4.1.8.2); gap SF-PII-key-formula) identifies RΓ(A', G) with RΓ(W(A'), 𝕄(G_{A'}))^{V=1}, which satisfies the hyperdescent by PF.3/dieudonne-side-arc-descent.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.5.1 and its proof, pp. 68–69; announced as Theorem 1.2.3, p. 6
sources.match: Flat cohomology and flat cohomology with supports of perfectoid rings satisfy p-complete arc hyperdescent on perfectoid algebras, proved by excision to supports along p = 0, arc descent for the generic fibre, p-adic continuity, deformation theory down to the perfect ring (A/p)_red and the crystalline key formula.

acceptance: For G étale of order prime to p it is arc hyperdescent of étale cohomology on perfectoids.

For A = 𝒪_C and the cover by a product of rank-one valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields, it computes RΓ(𝒪_C, G) from the products, where it is concentrated in degree 0 by PF.3/product-valuation-local-analysis.

nodes.title: The key formula for flat cohomology of perfectoid rings
nodes.statement: For a prime p, a perfectoid ring A, a commutative finite locally free A-group G of p-power order and a closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA), there is an identification RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G))^{V=1}, functorial in A, G and Z (with the same ξ used to define V over all perfectoid A-algebras).
hypotheses: A perfectoid (one may assume A a ℤ_p-algebra); G of p-power order; Z closed in Spec(A/p).
proofSteps: Assume A a ℤ_p-algebra and, by passing to an inverse limit, Z the vanishing locus of finitely many elements.

Case A = ∏ A_i with A_i perfectoid valuation rings of rank ≤ 1 with algebraically closed fraction fields: Z is cut out by one a | p, with compatible roots a^♭ cutting out Z in Spec(A^♭/p^♭). PF.3/product-valuation-local-analysis gives H^i(A, G) = H^i(A[1/a], G) = 0 for i ≥ 1, surjectivity of V − 1 on 𝕄(G) and 𝕄(G)[1/[a^♭]], and the unique compatible square of degree-zero identifications; by the support sequences both sides are concentrated in degree 0 and identified, functorially by uniqueness.

General A: both sides satisfy hyperdescent for p-complete arc hypercovers with perfectoid terms (PF.3/flat-side-arc-descent and PF.3/dieudonne-side-arc-descent), and products as above form a basis of the p-complete arc topology of A (ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.11/complete-valuation-product-basis, CS24 Lemma 2.2.3, with the factors perfectoid by CS24 (2.1.2.3) and the product perfectoid by PerfectoidQuotients Q0/products-of-perfectoid-rings); conclude by descent along such a hypercover.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.1.1, (6.1.1.1) and its proof, p. 82; announced as (1.1.6), p. 4
sources.match: RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G))^{V=1} for perfectoid A, functorially, proved on products of perfectoid valuation rings and extended by p-complete arc hyperdescent of both sides.

acceptance: For A a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra and ξ = p it is the crystalline key formula RΓ_Z(A, G) ≅ RΓ_Z(W(A), 𝕄(G))^{V=1} (CS24 (4.1.8.2)).
For Z = Spec(A/p) and G = ℤ/p over a perfect A it is the Artin–Schreier description of RΓ(A, ℤ/p).

For perfect A of characteristic p, Z = Spec A and ξ = p, the formula recovers the absolute low-degree descriptions of PF.3/perfectoid-low-degree-cohomology. For mixed-characteristic A, Z = Spec(A/p) is a support condition and need not be all of Spec A; use the localization triangle instead of identifying it with absolute cohomology.

nodes.title: Purity for flat cohomology of perfectoid rings
nodes.statement: For a prime p, a perfectoid ring A, a commutative finite locally free A-group G of p-power order, a closed Z ⊂ Spec(A/pA) and an A-regular sequence a_1, …, a_d ∈ A vanishing on Z, H^i_Z(A, G) = 0 for i < d.
hypotheses: A perfectoid; a_1, …, a_d an A-regular sequence (EGA convention) whose members vanish on Z; G of p-power order.
proofSteps: By PF.3/key-formula and the long exact sequence of PF.3/dieudonne-side-complex, it suffices that H^i_Z(A_inf(A), 𝕄(G)) = 0 for i < d (6.1.2.1).
𝕄(G) is finitely presented of projective dimension ≤ 1 over A_inf(A) (PD.6/covariant-normalisation), so it suffices that H^i_Z(A_inf(A), A_inf(A)) = 0 for i < d + 1.

Let ξ generate ker θ and choose lifts ã_1, …, ã_d ∈ A_inf(A) of a_1, …, a_d ∈ A = A_inf(A)/ξ. Since ξ is a nonzerodivisor (PrismaticCohomology PR.0/ainf-prism) and the a_k are regular on A_inf(A)/ξ = A, the sequence ξ, ã_1, …, ã_d is A_inf(A)-regular; it vanishes on Z ⊂ Spec(A/p) ⊂ Spec A_inf(A), and PF.0/regular-sequence-support-vanishing concludes by decreasing induction along A_inf(A)/(ξ, ã_1, …, ã_j).

sources.locator: Theorem 6.1.2 and its proof, pp. 82–83; announced as Theorem 1.1.5, p. 4
sources.match: On a perfectoid ring, flat cohomology with supports vanishes below the length of a regular sequence vanishing on Z, by the key formula, projective dimension ≤ 1 of 𝕄(G) and the A_inf-regular sequence ξ, a_1, …, a_d.
The decisive point is that depth_Z(A) ≥ d implies depth_Z(A_inf(A)) ≥ d + 1 through ξ.

acceptance: For A a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra (ξ = p) it is the last step of PF.2/char-p-complete-intersection-purity.

For A = the p-adic completion of W(k)⟦x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − f) and Z the closed point, the regular sequence x_1, …, x_d gives H^i_Z(A, G) = 0 for i < d, the input to PF.4/flat-purity-regular.
For d = 0 nothing is asserted, and indeed H^0(𝔽_p, ℤ/p) = ℤ/p ≠ 0 for A = 𝔽_p and Z = Spec 𝔽_p; the degree i = d is analysed separately for the towers of PF.4/flat-purity-regular.

nodes.title: Regular sequences survive adic completion under bounded torsion
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring, a ∈ A and Â the a-adic completion. If a_1, …, a_n ∈ A is an A-regular sequence such that each A/(a_1, …, a_i), 0 ≤ i ≤ n, has bounded a^∞-torsion, then a_1, …, a_n is Â-regular and Â/(a_1, …, a_n) ≅ (A/(a_1, …, a_n))^∧ (a-adic completion).
hypotheses: A arbitrary commutative ring; bounded a^∞-torsion of a module M means M[a^∞] = M[a^N] for some N; regular sequences in the EGA sense.
proofSteps: Bounded a^∞-torsion makes derived and classical a-adic completion agree on each A/(a_1, …, a_{i−1}) (the a-adic form of DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1/bounded-torsion-criterion, which states it for p; requested from DD.1 for an arbitrary element a), so the derived completion of 0 → A/(a_1, …, a_{i−1}) → A/(a_1, …, a_{i−1}) → A/(a_1, …, a_i) → 0 (first map multiplication by a_i) is the classical one and stays exact.
The resulting short exact sequences of completions show inductively that a_i is a nonzerodivisor on Â/(a_1, …, a_{i−1}) = (A/(a_1, …, a_{i−1}))^∧ and identify the quotients.

sources.match: Under bounded a^∞-torsion of all partial quotients, a regular sequence stays regular in the a-adic completion and completion commutes with the quotient, because derived and classical completions agree.

acceptance: For A Noetherian every finite module has bounded a^∞-torsion, so the lemma applies to every regular sequence.
For A = ℤ_p[x], a = p and the sequence x, it gives ℤ_p⟨x⟩/(x) = ℤ_p.
In CS24 it is applied to A = R̃_∞ = W(k)⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − f) with a = p and to A/(f_1^{1/p^∞}, …, f_n^{1/p^∞}), whose p^∞-torsion is killed by a fixed p^N.

nodes.title: Purity for flat cohomology of local complete intersections
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) that is a complete intersection and a commutative finite flat R-group G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < dim R.
hypotheses: R Noetherian local complete intersection (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3/complete-intersections); G commutative finite flat (equivalently finite locally free, R being local).
proofSteps: Decompose G into primary parts. If the order of the part is invertible in R, PF.1/etale-depth-virtual-dimension applies with vdim(R) = dim R; so assume G of p-power order with p = char(R/𝔪) > 0.

Excision to the completion (CS24 Corollary 5.4.5; gap SF-PII-excision) allows R 𝔪-adically complete; by the Cohen structure theorem with a Cohen ring C(k) (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/cohen-series-presentation) R ≅ R̃/J with R̃ = C(k)⟦x_1, …, x_N⟧ unramified complete regular local, and J is generated by a regular sequence f_1, …, f_n ∈ 𝔪̃ because R is a complete intersection and this property does not depend on the regular presentation (Stacks 09Q1; requested from R03.3). Argue by induction on i for all R at once.

Residue extension: the regular finite flat system R̃_j of CS24 Lemma 3.1.1(a) (gap PQ-PII-towers), PF.2/finite-flat-cover-reduction, a limit argument (PF.0, API limit) and Corollary 5.4.5 again reduce to R̃ with algebraically closed residue field.

Perfectoid tower: Lemma 3.1.1(b) (gap PQ-PII-towers) supplies a faithfully flat R̃-algebra R̃_∞ = W(k)⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − f) with perfectoid p-adic completion, and the same reductions bring us to H^i_𝔪(R̃_∞/(f_1, …, f_n), G) = 0 for i < dim R. By CS24 Corollary 5.3.8 (gap SF-PII-continuity) and PF.4/completion-regular-sequence replace R̃_∞ by its completion: it suffices to treat every p-torsion-free perfectoid A, p-completely faithfully flat over R̃; such A is R̃-flat (CS24 Lemma 6.2.1, Yekutieli; request to DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1), so f_1, …, f_n is A-regular.

Roots: André's lemma (PerfectoidQuotients Q3/andre-flatness-lemma, BS22 Theorem 7.14, CS24 footnote 25) gives a p-completely faithfully flat perfectoid A → A' containing compatible p-power roots of the f_i; Corollary 5.5.3 with Theorem 5.4.4 (gap SF-PII-excision) and PF.4/completion-regular-sequence give the descent spectral sequence whose terms are the completed tensor powers of A' (perfectoid by PerfectoidQuotients Q0/completed-perfectoid-tensor-products), so assume the f_i^{1/p^∞} lie in A.

PF.2/root-extraction-comparison with a limit argument reduces to H^i_𝔪(A/(f_1^{1/p^∞}, …, f_n^{1/p^∞}), G) = 0 for i < dim R. A fixed power p^N kills the p^∞-torsion of all A/(f^{1/p^{m}}, r_1, …, r_j) for an R-regular sequence r_1, …, r_{dim R} (Stacks 07DV and R̃-flatness), so PF.4/completion-regular-sequence keeps r_1, …, r_{dim R} regular on the p-adic completion of A/(f^{1/p^∞}), which is perfectoid (PerfectoidQuotients Q0/completed-root-stable-quotients). PF.3/perfectoid-purity and Corollary 5.3.8 conclude.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.2.3 and its proof, pp. 83–84; announced as Theorem 1.1.1, p. 3
sources.match: For Noetherian local complete intersections and commutative finite flat G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 below dim R, reduced to the perfectoid purity theorem through completion, residue and perfectoid towers, André's lemma and the root-extraction lemma.

nodes.title: Purity for finite étale coefficients below the virtual dimension
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) and a commutative finite étale R-group G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i < vdim(R).
hypotheses: R Noetherian local, arbitrary; G finite étale commutative of any order.
proofSteps: The proof of PF.1/etale-depth-virtual-dimension settles the part of G of order invertible in R and, for the rest, reduces (strict henselization, completion, closed-cover reduction, which work for any finite étale G) to G = ℤ/p with p = char(R/𝔪) > 0 and R = R̃/(f) a hypersurface.

A hypersurface in a regular local ring is a complete intersection with vdim(R) = dim R (PF.1/virtual-dimension), so PF.4/flat-purity-complete-intersection gives H^i_𝔪(R, ℤ/p) = 0 for i < dim R = vdim(R).

nodes.title: Flat purity fails below the virtual dimension for non-étale coefficients
nodes.statement: Let R = 𝔽_p⟦x, y, z, t⟧/(x^2, y^2, xz − yt). Then vdim(R) = 1, and the element xy ∈ R is nonzero, satisfies (xy)^p = 0 and is killed by the maximal ideal; hence it defines a nonzero element of H^0_𝔪(R, α_p). So PF.4/flat-purity-complete-intersection does not extend from complete intersections to rings of given virtual dimension for G = α_p.
hypotheses: p any prime; R as displayed (dimension 2, not a complete intersection).
proofSteps: vdim(R) = 4 − 3 = 1 because x^2, y^2, xz − yt are minimal generators (PF.1/virtual-dimension).

xy ≠ 0 in R (a monomial basis computation), (xy)^p = 0 since x^2 = 0, and x·xy = y·xy = 0, z·xy = y·(xz) = y^2t = 0, t·xy = x·(yt) = x^2z = 0; thus xy is supported at 𝔪, i.e. lies in ker(α_p(R) → α_p(U_R)) = H^0_𝔪(R, α_p) (PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports).

sources.match: For 𝔽_p⟦x, y, z, t⟧/(x^2, y^2, xz − yt) the nonzero element xy dies on the punctured spectrum and gives a nonzero class in H^0_𝔪(R, α_p), so vdim cannot replace dim in Theorem 6.2.3.

acceptance: By PF.4/etale-purity-virtual-dimension, H^0_𝔪(R, ℤ/p) = 0 for the same R, so the failure is specific to non-étale G.
The same element lies in H^0_𝔪(R, 𝔾_a), so depth_𝔪(R) = 0.

nodes.title: Purity for flat cohomology of regular local rings in degree dim R
nodes.statement: For a regular local ring (R, 𝔪) that is not a field and a commutative finite flat R-group G, H^i_𝔪(R, G) = 0 for i ≤ dim R.
hypotheses: R regular local of dimension d ≥ 1; G commutative finite flat.
proofSteps: PF.4/flat-purity-complete-intersection gives i < d; it remains to treat i = d. For the parts of G of order invertible in R, absolute purity (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §0.10) gives vanishing below 2d > d; so assume G of p-power order with p = char(R/𝔪) > 0.

Embed G into an abelian scheme B (Raynaud's embedding, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/raynaud-abelian-embedding, as in BBM 3.1.1; R is local), so G ⊂ B[p^n] when p^n kills G; the long exact sequence with PF.4/flat-purity-complete-intersection for the finite locally free cokernel B[p^n]/G reduces to G = B[p^n], and the filtration by the B[p^i], with graded pieces ≅ B[p], to G = B[p], the p-torsion of the p-divisible group H = B[p^∞].

Complete R using gap SF-PII-excision. At the boundary degree d, use PF.0 finite faithfully flat descent, together with the already proved CI vanishing H^t = 0 for t < d on localizations of the self-tensor products. These local rings are complete intersections: they are finite flat over the regular base with zero-dimensional complete-intersection fibres. The spectral sequence gives an injection H^d_𝔪(R,G) → H^d_{𝔪R′}(R′,G). It therefore permits the residue-field tower of PerfectoidSpaces P7.16a (CS24 Lemma 3.1.1(a)), followed by continuity and completion. This uses the descent spectral sequence at degree d, not the n < dim R hypothesis of PF.2/finite-flat-cover-reduction.

Now the residue field k is algebraically closed and R ≅ W(k)⟦x_1,…,x_d⟧/(p − f), with f = x_1 or f ∈ (p,x_1,…,x_d)^2; f = 0 includes equal characteristic. Use the finite flat regular tower of PerfectoidSpaces P7.17 in mixed characteristic and the ordinary perfection tower in characteristic p. Boundary-degree descent as above reduces to the colimit; gap SF-PII-continuity then allows its perfectoid p-adic completion R̂_∞. Complete flatness (request DD.1) keeps x_1,…,x_d regular. The explicit tilt-completion description remains in the narrowed gap PQ-PII-towers.

The pd ≤ 1 module estimate (6.1.2.1) gives H^i_Z(A_inf(R̂_∞),𝕄(G)) = 0 for i < d, not i < d + 1. Its degree d − 1 vanishing and PF.3/key-formula identify H^d_Z(R̂_∞,G) with ker(V − 1 on H^d_Z(A_inf(R̂_∞),𝕄(G))). Because G = H[p], 𝕄(G) is a finite free module over the local tilt R̂_∞^♭; thus this kernel is computed on the tilt.

The tilt is the f-adic completion of k⟦(x_1^♭)^{1/p^∞},…,(x_d^♭)^{1/p^∞}⟧. The completion agrees with that ring modulo every tuple ((x_1^♭)^{n_1},…,(x_d^♭)^{n_d}), so its top local cohomology has k-basis the monomials with all exponents negative in ℤ[1/p]. An element has finite support in this basis. Choose its smallest signed total exponent a_1 + ⋯ + a_d. Frobenius inverse divides this negative sum by p and matrix coefficients have nonnegative exponents, so every surviving term after applying V has strictly larger total exponent. Thus V has no nonzero fixed vector.

The residue-field and perfectoid towers over complete regular local rings used in the reduction.

acceptance: For R a discrete valuation ring (d = 1) with fraction field K and G = μ_p, H^0_𝔪 = H^1_𝔪 = 0 amounts to μ_p(R) = μ_p(K) and injectivity of R^×/R^{×p} = H^1(R, μ_p) → K^×/K^{×p}; both hold because R is integrally closed.

The field case fails, for example for the constant nonzero group G = ℤ/n with n > 1: U_K = ∅ and H^0_𝔪(K,G) = G(K) = ℤ/n. A nontrivial group scheme need not have nontrivial K-points (μ_p in characteristic p), so specify the coefficient group.

For R = 𝔽_p⟦x, y⟧ and G = α_p: H^2_𝔪(R, α_p) = ker(F : H^2_𝔪(R) → H^2_𝔪(R)) (as H^1_𝔪(R) = 0), which vanishes because Frobenius is flat on the regular ring R (Kunz) and hence injective on local cohomology.

nodes.title: Global purity for flat cohomology with finite flat coefficients
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme, G a commutative finite locally free X-group, d an integer and Z ⊂ X a closed subset such that X ∖ Z → X is quasi-compact and, for every z ∈ Z, the local ring 𝒪_{X,z} is either a complete intersection of dimension ≥ d or regular of dimension ≥ max(d − 1, 1). Then H^i(X, G) → H^i(X ∖ Z, G) is injective for i < d and bijective for i < d − 1; equivalently H^i_Z(X, G) = 0 for i < d.
hypotheses: X arbitrary scheme; the local rings at points of Z are Noetherian by hypothesis.

The regular case requires dimension ≥ max(d − 1, 1), not merely ≥ d − 1: for d = 1 the source's condition admits fields, for which the statement is false (PurityForFlatCohomology/E1, after PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24/E1).
proofSteps: The assertion is H^i_Z(X, G) = 0 for i < d. By the local-to-global spectral sequence of PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports and quasi-compactness of X ∖ Z → X (stalks of ℋ^j_Z are cohomology with supports of strict henselizations) reduce to X strictly henselian local with Z ≠ ∅; the strict henselization of a complete intersection (regular ring) is a complete intersection (regular ring) of the same dimension, by the flat-local criterion (R → R^sh is flat with residue fibre a field), and so are the localizations at the generic points of Z used below (requested from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3); X is Noetherian.

Noetherian induction on Z: if Z ≠ {𝔪}, choose a generic point z of Z and open neighbourhoods U of z. The Mayer–Vietoris sequence for U ∪ (X ∖ Z) (PF.0, API mayerVietoris) and, in the limit over U, the local theorems for 𝒪_{X,z} — PF.4/flat-purity-complete-intersection (vanishing below dim ≥ d) and PF.4/flat-purity-regular (vanishing up to dim ≥ max(d − 1, 1)) — show that H^i(U, G) → H^i(U ∖ Z, G) is bijective for i < d − 1 and injective for i = d − 1, so classes extend over (or die on) U ∪ (X ∖ Z) and Z may be replaced by Z ∖ U.
At Z = {𝔪} the vanishing is exactly the local theorems.

sources.match: Injectivity below d and bijectivity below d − 1 of restriction to X ∖ Z for finite locally free commutative G when the local rings along Z are complete intersections of dimension ≥ d or regular of dimension ≥ d − 1, by the local-to-global spectral sequence, Mayer–Vietoris shrinking of Z and the local purity theorems.

For X = Spec k ⊔ Spec k, Z one point and d = 1 the uncorrected hypothesis would allow 𝒪_{X,z} = k and the map H^0(X, G) → H^0(X ∖ Z, G) is not injective: the corrected bound max(d − 1, 1) excludes it.
For a smooth variety X over a field and Z of codimension ≥ c, it gives H^i(X, μ_p) ≅ H^i(X ∖ Z, μ_p) for i < c − 1, even in characteristic p.

nodes.title: Auslander's freeness criterion through endomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let R be a regular local ring and M a finitely generated reflexive R-module such that Hom_R(M, M) ≅ M^{⊕r} as R-modules for some r. Then M is free.
hypotheses: R regular local; M finitely generated and reflexive (Mathlib Module.IsReflexive).
proofSteps: The exact freeness criterion used here is explicitly invoked in CS24, proof of Theorem 7.1.3, p. 88; the hypotheses in this node are the reflexive finite-module case of that input. The case M=0 is immediate; for M nonzero the endomorphism isomorphism forces r>0.

The proposed proof by depth induction in the original plan was not justified: the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula alone does not show that End_R(M)≅M^{⊕r} forces maximal depth. The original Auslander Theorem 1.3 proof could not be read from the public publisher endpoint. Its homological freeness argument is therefore an explicit proof obligation, gap AUSLANDER-FREENESS, rather than a claimed routine reduction. This node retains ownership of the criterion; its application in torsor-gerbe-purity uses the criterion exactly as stated in CS24.

sources.match: A result of Auslander, which uses the regularity of the base, reduces flatness of j_*(𝒪_Y) to an isomorphism between its endomorphism module and a direct sum of copies of itself.
Over a regular local ring a finitely generated module whose endomorphism module is a direct sum of copies of it is free (not read; cited through CS24 p. 88).

acceptance: For M = R^n the hypothesis holds with r = n and M is free.

Over a non-regular ring reflexivity and maximal depth do not force freeness: over the A_1 singularity R = k⟦x, y, z⟧/(xz − y^2) the ideal M = (x, y) is reflexive of rank one and of depth 2 = dim R but not free; here End_R(M) ≅ R is not a sum of copies of M, so the criterion does not apply.
For R a discrete valuation ring, finitely generated reflexive modules are free and the criterion is automatic.

nodes.title: Purity for torsors and gerbes under finite locally free groups (Moret-Bailly)
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme, G a finite locally free X-group (not necessarily commutative) and Z ⊂ X a closed subset such that j : X ∖ Z → X is quasi-compact and each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, is regular of dimension ≥ 2. Then pullback is an equivalence from G-torsors over X to G_{X∖Z}-torsors over X ∖ Z. More generally, for every G-gerbe 𝔅 over X, 𝔅(X) → 𝔅(X ∖ Z) is an equivalence of groupoids; in particular ker(H^2(X, G) → H^2(X ∖ Z, G)) is trivial for the nonabelian H^2.
hypotheses: X arbitrary; G finite locally free, possibly noncommutative; regularity of dimension ≥ 2 at every point of Z (Remark 7.1.4 of CS24 expects but does not prove the complete-intersection-of-dimension-≥-3 variant).
proofSteps: Étale locally every G-gerbe is BG (BG is smooth), so étale descent reduces to G-torsors.

By glueing the claim is Zariski-local; localizing at a point of Z and spreading out (quasi-compactness of j) reduce to X local Noetherian with Z ≠ ∅. Full faithfulness: torsors are affine over X and depth_Z(X) ≥ 2, so isomorphisms extend uniquely (PF.0/hartogs-regular-sequence(b), EGA IV 5.10.5).

Essential surjectivity: by Noetherian induction and spreading out assume Z is the closed point. For a G_{X∖Z}-torsor Y, j_*(𝒪_Y) is a coherent 𝒪_X-algebra (EGA IV 5.11.4; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.4); it suffices that it is flat, for then the torsor structure extends by full faithfulness to Spec_X j_*(𝒪_Y).

Flatness: by PF.5/auslander-endomorphism-freeness it suffices that Hom(j_*𝒪_Y, j_*𝒪_Y) ≅ (j_*𝒪_Y)^{⊕r}; both sides are reflexive (depth ≥ 2), so it suffices to check over X ∖ Z, where the action map gives Hom(𝒪_G ⊗ 𝒪_Y, 𝒪_Y) ≅ Hom(𝒪_Y, 𝒪_Y) through the isomorphism G × Y ≅ Y × Y, with 𝒪_G free of rank r over 𝒪_X.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.1.3 and its proof, pp. 87–88; Remark 7.1.4, p. 88
sources.match: Moret-Bailly's purity for torsors under finite locally free groups over regular schemes of dimension ≥ 2 along Z, and its extension to gerbes and the nonabelian H^2, by Hartogs for full faithfulness and Auslander's criterion for flatness of the pushed-forward algebra.

acceptance: For X = Spec R regular local of dimension 2 and G = ℤ/n with n invertible this is Zariski–Nagata purity for ℤ/n-torsors.
For G = α_p over 𝔽_p⟦x, y⟧, every α_p-torsor on U_R extends, consistent with PF.4/flat-purity-regular in degree 1.

nodes.title: Parafactorial and geometrically parafactorial local rings
nodes.statement: A local ring (R, 𝔪) is parafactorial if, with X = Spec R and U = U_R, pullback is an equivalence from invertible sheaves on X to invertible sheaves on U; equivalently Γ(X, 𝒪) → Γ(U, 𝒪) is bijective and Pic(U) = 0. It is geometrically parafactorial if its strict henselization is parafactorial. A pair (X, Y) of a scheme and a closed subset is parafactorial if for every open V ⊂ X restriction of invertible sheaves from V to V ∖ Y is an equivalence.
hypotheses: R local (Noetherian where depth is used); Pic(U) is Tau Ceti's LineBundleClass of U.
proofSteps: The equivalence of the two forms: every invertible sheaf on the local scheme X is trivial, so essential surjectivity is Pic(U) = 0 and full faithfulness is bijectivity of Γ(X, 𝒪) → Γ(U, 𝒪) (EGA IV 21.13.3, 21.13.8).
For R Noetherian, bijectivity on global sections is depth R ≥ 2 (EGA IV 21.13.4 and 5.10.5; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.6), so parafactorial rings have dimension ≥ 2 (21.13.9(i)).

sources.locator: Définition 21.13.7, Proposition 21.13.8, Exemples 21.13.9 (i)–(ii), pp. 316–317; Corollaire 21.13.6 (iii), p. 316; Proposition 21.13.10, p. 319; 21.13.12.1, pp. 320–321
sources.match: Parafactoriality of a local ring through the punctured spectrum, its characterisation by depth ≥ 2 and Pic(U) = 0, the dimension bound, factorial rings of dimension ≥ 2 being parafactorial, descent along faithfully flat quasi-compact maps and from the completion, and the pointwise criterion for pairs.
Geometric parafactoriality is parafactoriality of the strict henselization; geometrically factorial rings of dimension ≥ 2 and complete intersections of dimension ≥ 4 are geometrically parafactorial.

sources.locator: Exposé XI §3, Définitions 3.1–3.2 and Lemme 3.6, pp. 101–102
sources.match: A pair (X, Z) is parafactorial when restriction of locally free modules of rank one from V to V ∖ Z is an equivalence for every open V, a local ring when its pair with the closed point is, and parafactoriality descends along faithfully flat quasi-compact maps.
The Grothendieck–Lefschetz theorem (SGA 2 XI 3.13(ii)) is used in the form: the Picard group of the punctured spectrum of a local complete intersection of dimension ≥ 4 vanishes.

nodes.title: Gabber's conjecture on the local Picard group
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) that is a complete intersection of dimension ≥ 3, Pic(U_R)_tors = 0. If R has dimension ≥ 4 or is regular (of any dimension ≥ 2), then Pic(U_R) = 0.
hypotheses: R Noetherian local complete intersection; U_R its punctured spectrum (PF.0).
proofSteps: Dimension ≥ 4: SGA 2 XI 3.13(ii), planned upstream as DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §6.9 (localCI_parafactorial).

Regular R: a line bundle on U_R is trivial iff it extends to R; extend it as a coherent module and take the determinant of a finite free resolution (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §6.9, punctured regular local spectra), or use factoriality of R and Weil divisors.

Torsion: for n ≥ 1, PF.4/flat-purity-complete-intersection (dim R ≥ 3, so H^1_𝔪 = H^2_𝔪 = 0 for μ_n) makes H^1(R, μ_n) → H^1(U_R, μ_n) bijective. A class of Pic(U_R)[n] lifts to H^1(U_R, μ_n) by the fppf Kummer sequence (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11), hence comes from H^1(R, μ_n), whose image in H^1(R, 𝔾_m) = Pic(R) = 0 vanishes (the source writes n ≥ 0 where n ≥ 1 is meant, PurityForFlatCohomology/E4).
