sources.match: Pic(U_R)_tors = 0 for complete intersections of dimension ≥ 3, and Pic(U_R) = 0 in dimension ≥ 4 or for regular R, from purity for μ_n, the Kummer sequence and SGA 2 XI 3.13(ii).

Part (i): regular local rings are factorial (Auslander–Buchsbaum), hence parafactorial in dimension ≥ 2; part (ii), the local Grothendieck–Lefschetz theorem: complete intersections of dimension ≥ 4 are parafactorial.

acceptance: For the three-dimensional node R = k⟦x, y, z, w⟧/(xy − zw), Pic(U_R) ≅ ℤ (generated by the ideal (x, z)) is torsion free and nonzero: dimension 3 gives only torsion vanishing.

Dimension 2 complete intersections can have torsion: let S be the local ring at the vertex of the affine cone over a smooth plane cubic over ℂ. Then S is a two-dimensional hypersurface and Pic(U_S)_tors is infinite (CS24 Remark 7.2.6).

nodes.title: Purity fails for Cohen–Macaulay rings
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 3 let R = ℂ⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧^{ℤ/2} with ℤ/2 acting by x_i ↦ −x_i. Then R is a Cohen–Macaulay normal local domain of dimension n, ℂ⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ restricts to a nontrivial ℤ/2-torsor over U_R, and its class is a nonzero element of Pic(U_R)[2]. Hence PF.5/local-picard-torsion-vanishing and PF.4/flat-purity-complete-intersection fail for Cohen–Macaulay rings.
hypotheses: n ≥ 3 (for n = 2, R is the A_1 singularity, also with nonzero Pic(U_R)[2]).
proofSteps: R → ℂ⟦x⟧ is the normalization of R in a quadratic extension of fraction fields, free of fixed points off the closed point, hence a ℤ/2-torsor over U_R; it is connected, so nontrivial.
R is a direct summand of ℂ⟦x⟧ (anti-invariants as complement), so a system of parameters of R is one of ℂ⟦x⟧ and R is Cohen–Macaulay.
depth R = n ≥ 2 gives R^× = H^0(U_R, 𝔾_m), and units of R are squares (Hensel, residue field ℂ), so the Kummer sequence identifies H^1(U_R, μ_2) with Pic(U_R)[2] and the torsor gives a nonzero class.

Use H^1(R,μ_2) = 0 and the support long exact sequence to send this nonzero punctured torsor injectively into H^2_𝔪(R,μ_2). It is this degree-two class, not degree one, that violates flat CI purity for n ≥ 3.

sources.match: The ℤ/2-invariants of a power series ring form a Cohen–Macaulay normal domain over whose punctured spectrum the power series ring is a nontrivial ℤ/2-torsor, giving 2-torsion in Pic(U_R); so Theorems 7.2.1 and 1.1.1 fail for Cohen–Macaulay rings.

acceptance: For n = 3, R is the cone over the Veronese surface: Cohen–Macaulay of dimension 3 but not a complete intersection, with Pic(U_R) ⊃ ℤ/2.

H^2_𝔪(R,μ_2) ≠ 0: the nontrivial μ_2-torsor on U_R cannot come from H^1(R,μ_2) = R^×/R^{×2} = 0, so its localization boundary is nonzero. Since n ≥ 3, this contradicts the below-dimension CI bound. H^1_𝔪(R,μ_2) is zero here.

nodes.title: Picard groups of global complete intersections
nodes.statement: For a field k and a global complete intersection X ⊂ ℙ^n_k of dimension ≥ 2, (Pic(X)/ℤ·[𝒪(1)])_tors = 0. If dim X ≥ 3, then Pic(X) is free of rank one, generated by [𝒪(1)]. The torsion condition cannot be dropped in dimension 2 (the quadric surface has Pic ≅ ℤ^2), nor the dimension lowered (an elliptic curve over an algebraically closed field has infinite Pic_tors).
hypotheses: X = Proj k[x_0, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_{n−d}) with f_i homogeneous forming a regular sequence, d = dim X.
proofSteps: The homogeneous coordinate ring R = k[x_0, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_{n−d}) satisfies R ≅ ⊕_{m≥0} Γ(X, 𝒪_X(m)) compatibly with the gradings. A line bundle L defines the finite graded module M_L = ⊕_{m≥0} Γ(X, L(m)) whose restriction to Spec R_𝔪 ∖ {𝔪} (𝔪 = (x_0, …, x_n)) is a line bundle L̃, with L̃ ⊗ L̃' ≅ (L ⊗ L')~ (EGA II 3.2.4, 3.2.6, 3.4.3, 3.4.4); if L̃ is trivial then M_L is free and L ≅ 𝒪(m). This gives an injection Pic(X)/ℤ·[𝒪(1)] → Pic(U_{R_𝔪}).

R_𝔪 is a complete intersection of dimension d + 1 ≥ 3, so PF.5/local-picard-torsion-vanishing gives the torsion statement; for d ≥ 3, dim R_𝔪 ≥ 4 gives Pic(U_{R_𝔪}) = 0, hence Pic(X) = ℤ·[𝒪(1)], free since 𝒪(1) has positive degree (SGA 2 XII 3.7 for the original argument).
Sharpness: the quadric xw − yz = 0 is ℙ^1 × ℙ^1 with Pic = ℤ^2, and Pic of an elliptic curve over an algebraically closed field contains its torsion points.

sources.locator: Corollary 7.2.3 and its proof, p. 89; Remark 7.2.4, p. 90
sources.match: Torsion-freeness of Pic(X)/ℤ[𝒪(1)] for global complete intersections of dimension ≥ 2 and freeness on 𝒪(1) in dimension ≥ 3, via the affine cone and Theorem 7.2.1; sharpness by the quadric surface and elliptic curves.
For a complete intersection of dimension ≥ 3 in projective space, Pic(X) is free on the class of 𝒪_X(1), by induction on the number of hypersurfaces.

acceptance: For a cubic threefold X ⊂ ℙ^4 (a hypersurface of dimension 3), Pic(X) = ℤ[𝒪(1)].
For the quadric surface, Pic(X)/ℤ[𝒪(1)] ≅ ℤ is torsion free but nonzero.
For a plane cubic curve (dim 1) the torsion of Pic(X)/ℤ[𝒪(1)] is infinite over k̄, so dim ≥ 2 is needed.

nodes.title: Torsion of 𝔾_m-cohomology for schemes with factorial strict henselizations (Grothendieck)
nodes.statement: Let X be a Noetherian integral scheme with function field K. (a) If every strict henselization 𝒪^sh_{X,x̄} is factorial, then H^i_ét(X, 𝔾_m) is torsion for every i ≥ 2. (b) If X is regular, then H^2_ét(X, 𝔾_m) → H^2_ét(K, 𝔾_m) is injective; in particular H^2_ét(X, 𝔾_m) is torsion.
hypotheses: X Noetherian integral; in (b) X regular, so its strict henselizations are regular, hence factorial (Auslander–Buchsbaum).
proofSteps: Let g : Spec K → X. Under geometric local factoriality the divisor sequence 0 → 𝔾_m → g_*𝔾_{m,K} → ⊕_{x∈X^{(1)}}(i_x)_*ℤ → 0 is exact on X_ét. This is Grothendieck 1966, §1, Proposition 1.4, with the divisor sheaf identified by factoriality.

For a point inclusion i_x and any étale abelian sheaf on Spec k(x), positive direct images and positive-degree cohomology of its pushforward are torsion (Grothendieck Lemma 1.1). One way to see the all-degree assertion is to rationalize the Leray spectral sequence: higher direct images are torsion, their cohomology is torsion on Noetherian X, and field cohomology is torsion in positive degrees. Apply this to g and to each i_x. Cohomology commutes with the direct sum on Noetherian X, so the divisor sheaf also has torsion cohomology in every positive degree.

The divisor long exact sequence now gives H^i(X,𝔾_m) torsion for every i ≥ 2. For injectivity in degree two, H^1(X,(i_x)_*ℤ) = 0 (Lemma 1.9) and R^1g_*𝔾_m = 0 by Hilbert 90. Consequently H^2(X,𝔾_m) injects into H^2(X,g_*𝔾_m), which injects into H^2(K,𝔾_m) by Leray. This is Corollary 1.8, not an assertion that the latter injection holds in all degrees.

Regular local rings and their strict henselizations are factorial; import this commutative algebra through the R03.3 contract. The source read directly for the divisor argument is the freely available Bourbaki 1966 version, not an unread copy of Dix exposés.

sources.match: For the strictly local Noetherian integral X reached there, factoriality makes H^i(X, 𝔾_m) and H^i(X ∖ Z, 𝔾_m) torsion for i ≥ 2 (Grothendieck, Le groupe de Brauer II, 1.4).
For Noetherian integral regular X with function field K, H^2(X, 𝔾_m) → H^2(K, 𝔾_m) is injective, so H^2(X, 𝔾_m) is torsion (Grothendieck, Brauer II, 1.8).

sources.locator: Le groupe de Brauer II, Proposition 1.4 and Corollaire 1.8
sources.match: Torsion and injectivity into the generic point (not read; cited through CS24 p. 93 and C19 p. 7).

sources.locator: Le groupe de Brauer II, §1, Lemma 1.1, Proposition 1.4, Lemmas 1.6 and 1.9, Corollary 1.8, pp. 290–293
sources.match: Directly read: torsion in all higher degrees follows from the divisor sheaf; the degree-two map to the generic point is injective under geometric local factoriality.

acceptance: For X = Spec of a regular local ring of dimension 1 (a DVR), (b) is the injectivity Br(R) → Br(K).
For X = 𝔸^2_ℂ, H^2(X, 𝔾_m) = Br(𝔸^2_ℂ) = 0 is torsion.
For X = Spec K a field both parts say that H^i(K, 𝔾_m) is torsion for i ≥ 1, as Galois cohomology in positive degrees is torsion.

nodes.title: Vector bundles and Azumaya algebras on punctured regular surfaces
nodes.statement: Let R be a regular local ring of dimension 2. Pullback is an equivalence from vector bundles on Spec R to vector bundles on U_R, and from Azumaya algebras on Spec R to Azumaya algebras on U_R; hence Br(R) → Br(U_R) is bijective for the Azumaya Brauer groups. If R is strictly henselian, then H^2_ét(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0.
hypotheses: R regular local of dimension exactly 2; Br is SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.22's SchemeBrauerGroup.
proofSteps: Full faithfulness is Hartogs (depth R = 2; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.6, coherent_hartogs). For a vector bundle E on U_R, j_*E is coherent and reflexive (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.6, reflexive_extension_normal), hence of depth 2 = dim R at the closed point, hence free by the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula (PurityOfBranchLocus §0.3).

For an Azumaya algebra A on U_R, j_*A is a free algebra; the map j_*A ⊗ (j_*A)^op → End(j_*A) of free modules is an isomorphism on U_R, hence on Spec R by Hartogs, so j_*A is Azumaya (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.22, azumaya_equivalent_conditions).

If R is strictly henselian, Br(R) = Br(k) = 0 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.22, brauer_henselian_local, k separably closed), so Br(U_R) = 0; H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) is torsion (PF.5/gm-cohomology-torsion(b), U_R regular integral) and its torsion is Br(U_R) because U_R is regular of dimension ≤ 2 (Grothendieck, Brauer II, Br = Br′ in dimension ≤ 2; recorded gap SF-PII-brauer).

sources.match: For regular local rings of dimension 2 pullback is an equivalence on vector bundles and on Azumaya algebras between R and U_R (Grothendieck, Brauer III, 6.1 b)), giving Br(R) ≅ Br(U_R).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.3 case (i), p. 2; proof of Theorem 5.3, p. 12
sources.match: The case dim R = 2 of the strict-local purity H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0 follows from the equivalence of vector bundles on Spec R and on U_R.

sources.match: Vector bundles and Azumaya algebras extend over the closed point of a regular local ring of dimension 2 (not read; cited through CS24 p. 90 and C19 p. 2).

In dimension 3 vector bundles need not extend: on U_R for R = k⟦x, y, z⟧ the syzygy bundle of (x, y, z) is not free, although Br(R) ≅ Br(U_R) still holds (PF.5/brauer-purity-complete-intersection).
Regularity is needed: over the A_1 singularity the rank-one reflexive module (x, y) restricts to a nontrivial line bundle on U_R.

nodes.title: Gabber's conjecture on the Brauer group of local complete intersections
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪) that is either a complete intersection of dimension ≥ 4 or regular of dimension ≥ 2, pullback Br(R) → Br(U_R) is bijective, where Br is the Brauer group of Azumaya algebras.
hypotheses: R Noetherian local; Br(X) = ⋃_n im(H^1(X, PGL_n) → H^2(X, 𝔾_m)_tors), SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.22.
proofSteps: By Gabber and de Jong, Br(X) = H^2(X, 𝔾_m)_tors for X with an ample line bundle, in particular for X quasi-affine such as Spec R and U_R (recorded gap SF-PII-brauer; SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.22 constructs Br → Br′).

Pic(R) = 0 and Pic(U_R) = 0 (PF.5/local-picard-torsion-vanishing), so the Kummer sequences give Br(R)[n] ≅ H^2(R, μ_n) and Br(U_R)[n] ≅ H^2(U_R, μ_n) for n ≥ 1 (the source writes n ≥ 0, PurityForFlatCohomology/E5; SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11).

Except for R regular of dimension 2, H^2(R, μ_n) ≅ H^2(U_R, μ_n) because H^2_𝔪 = H^3_𝔪 = 0: by PF.4/flat-purity-complete-intersection for complete intersections of dimension ≥ 4 and by PF.4/flat-purity-regular for regular rings of dimension ≥ 3.
For R regular of dimension 2 use PF.5/regular-dimension-two-extension.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.2.5 and its proof, p. 90; announced as Theorem 1.1.3(b), p. 3
sources.match: Br(R) ≅ Br(U_R) for complete intersections of dimension ≥ 4 or regular rings of dimension ≥ 2, via Gabber–de Jong, vanishing of Pic, the Kummer sequence, purity for μ_n, and Grothendieck's dimension-two case.

sources.match: The regular case: H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0 for strictly henselian regular R of dimension ≥ 2, i.e. Br(U_R) = Br(R) = 0 there.

For R = k⟦x_1, …, x_5⟧/(f) a hypersurface of dimension 4, Br(R) ≅ Br(U_R).
Dimension 3 complete intersections are excluded: PF.5/brauer-purity-sharpness gives a three-dimensional strictly henselian complete intersection with Br(R) = 0 and Br(U_R) infinite.

nodes.title: Sharpness of the dimension bound for Brauer purity
nodes.statement: Let S be the local ring at the vertex of the affine cone over a smooth plane cubic over ℂ. Then R = S^sh⟦x,y⟧/(xy) is a three-dimensional strictly henselian complete intersection with Br(R) = 0 and Br(U_R) infinite. With the Segre embedding of ℙ^1_ℂ × ℙ^1_ℂ instead, S has dimension 3 and R dimension 4; H^2(U_R,𝔾_m) has non-extendable, necessarily nontorsion classes.
hypotheses: In the elliptic case S is a two-dimensional normal local hypersurface over ℂ with infinite Pic(U_S)_tors. In the Segre case it is a three-dimensional normal hypersurface. Both R are strictly henselian complete intersections; the dimensions of the two examples differ.
proofSteps: Pic(U_S) → Pic(U_{S^sh}) is injective (Γ(U_S, L) is free for L in the kernel), so Pic(U_{S^sh})_tors is infinite while Pic(U_{S^sh⟦t⟧}) is finitely generated (Boutot 1978, V 4.9).

The exact sequence 0 → 𝔾_m → (i_{x=0})_*𝔾_m ⊕ (i_{y=0})_*𝔾_m → (i_{x=y=0})_*𝔾_m → 0 on Spec(R)_ét (Boutot 1978, IV 5.1) relates Br(U_R) to the Picard groups of the punctured spectra of the components and of their intersection, giving #Br(U_R) = ∞, whereas Br(R) = 0 because R is strictly henselian.

For the Segre cone, Pic(U_{S^sh}) has a free cyclic contribution. The same component sequence produces non-extendable classes in H^2(U_R,𝔾_m). Here H^2(R,𝔾_m) = 0 because R is strictly local. Since dim R = 4, Brauer purity identifies the torsion subgroup on U_R with Br(R) = 0; hence these nonzero classes are nontorsion. The general H^2 assertion cannot replace the torsion Brauer assertion.

sources.match: A three-dimensional strictly henselian complete intersection built from the cone over an elliptic curve has trivial Brauer group but infinite Brauer group of its punctured spectrum; the ℙ^1 × ℙ^1 variant gives non-extendable classes in H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m).

sources.locator: Chapitre IV, Lemme 5.1; Chapitre V, Corollaire 4.9
sources.match: The Mayer–Vietoris sequence for 𝔾_m along two components and finite generation of local Picard groups (not read; cited through CS24 p. 90).

Pic(U_S)_tors is infinite for the elliptic cone, matching the sharpness of PF.5/global-complete-intersection-picard in dimension 1.

nodes.title: Purity for groups of multiplicative type in degrees ≤ 2
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme, T a finite type X-group of multiplicative type and Z ⊂ X a closed subset with X ∖ Z → X quasi-compact. (a) If each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, is Noetherian and geometrically parafactorial, then H^0(X, T) ≅ H^0(X ∖ Z, T), H^1(X, T) ≅ H^1(X ∖ Z, T) and H^2(X, T) → H^2(X ∖ Z, T) is injective. (b) If each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, is a complete intersection of dimension ≥ 3 (resp. ≥ 4) or regular of dimension ≥ 2, then H^1(X, T)_tors ≅ H^1(X ∖ Z, T)_tors (resp. H^2(X, T)_tors ≅ H^2(X ∖ Z, T)_tors), where torsion means killed by a locally constant function. In particular, for Noetherian X with each 𝒪_{X,z} a complete intersection of dimension ≥ 4 or regular of dimension ≥ 2, H^2(X, 𝔾_m)_tors ≅ H^2(X ∖ Z, 𝔾_m)_tors.
hypotheses: X arbitrary; groups of multiplicative type over X are those of SGA 3 IX (recorded gap SF-PII-tori for their scheme-level theory); cohomology is fppf, equal to étale cohomology for smooth T.
α ∈ H^i(X, T)_tors iff X = ⊔_{n>0} X_n (clopens) with α|_{X_n} killed by n.
proofSteps: (a) It suffices that H^i_Z(X, T) = 0 for i ≤ 2. Parafactorial rings have depth ≥ 2 (PF.5/parafactorial-local-ring), so PF.0/hartogs-regular-sequence(b) gives i ≤ 1. By PF.0's local-to-global spectral sequence reduce to X strictly local, Noetherian, Z ≠ ∅; realizing T as the kernel of a map of tori, assume T = 𝔾_m; the claim is that j_*L is a line bundle for every line bundle L on X ∖ Z. By Noetherian induction and flat base change of j_*, pass to the strict henselization at a generic point of Z, where Z is the closed point and parafactoriality gives the claim.

(b) Injectivity follows from PF.0 Hartogs in degree one and from (a) in degree two. Hartogs also identifies clopens, so reduce to a class α killed by n > 0. After a clopen decomposition, choose m > 0 killing the torsion of the locally constant character module of T. Then [m] factors as T →^q S ↪ T, with S a torus, q an fppf epimorphism and kernel T[m]. The epimorphism [n]∘q : T → S has finite locally free kernel T[mn]. Since ([n]∘q)(α) = q(nα) = 0, the coefficient long exact sequence lifts α to H^i(X∖Z,T[mn]). This explains the reduction to finite coefficients; it does not assume T itself is n-torsion.

For these finite coefficients, the support local-to-global sequence, limits, Noetherian induction and Mayer–Vietoris reduce surjectivity to a strictly local ring with Z the closed point. PF.4 gives extension except in the regular dimension-two case. There use (a) for H^1; for H^2 reduce étale-locally to diagonalizable T and use Kummer with PF.5/brauer-purity-complete-intersection. The scheme character-module and torus embedding interfaces are requested in SF-PII-tori. The resulting extension in H^i(X,T) is torsion because the finite coefficient group is killed by mn.

The regular case for tori, with bijectivity of H^2 and injectivity of H^3 (PF.6/torus-purity).

For T = μ_n with n invertible, (b) in degree 1 is purity for μ_n-torsors.

nodes.title: Purity for groups of multiplicative type in higher degrees
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme, T a finite type X-group of multiplicative type, d ≥ 3 and Z ⊂ X a closed subset with X ∖ Z → X quasi-compact such that each 𝒪_{X,z}, z ∈ Z, is either a complete intersection of dimension ≥ d all of whose strict henselizations are factorial, or regular of dimension ≥ d − 1. Then H^i(X, T) → H^i(X ∖ Z, T) is injective for i < d and bijective for i < d − 1.
hypotheses: d ≥ 3; complete intersections whose local rings of height ≤ 3 are factorial are factorial (SGA 2 XI 3.14), e.g. regular ones.
proofSteps: It suffices that H^i_Z(X, T) = 0 for i < d. PF.0's local-to-global sequence reduces to X strictly local with Z ≠ ∅, so X is Noetherian and integral, and realizing T inside a torus reduces to T = 𝔾_m.

By PF.5/gm-cohomology-torsion(a), which uses factoriality of the strict henselizations, H^i(X, 𝔾_m) and H^i(X ∖ Z, 𝔾_m) are torsion for i ≥ 2; by PF.5/multiplicative-type-purity-low-degree(a), H^i(X, 𝔾_m) ≅ H^i(X ∖ Z, 𝔾_m) for i ≤ 1. Hence all H^i_Z(X, 𝔾_m) are torsion.
The vanishing H^i_Z(X, μ_n) = 0 for i < d from PF.5/global-flat-purity and the Kummer sequence then give H^i_Z(X, 𝔾_m)[n] = 0 and hence H^i_Z(X, 𝔾_m) = 0 for i < d.

sources.match: Injectivity below d and bijectivity below d − 1 for groups of multiplicative type along complete intersections of dimension ≥ d with factorial strict henselizations or regular rings of dimension ≥ d − 1, from torsion of 𝔾_m-cohomology and Theorem 7.1.2 for μ_n.

acceptance: For X regular and Z of codimension ≥ 2 (d = 3) it gives bijectivity of H^i(X, T) → H^i(X ∖ Z, T) for i ≤ 1 and injectivity for i = 2; for tori C19 Theorem 6.1 strengthens this to bijectivity for i ≤ 2 and injectivity for i = 3 (PF.6/torus-purity).
For T = μ_n it is PF.5/global-flat-purity.

nodes.title: Purity for the Brauer group of a punctured strictly henselian regular local ring
nodes.statement: For a strictly henselian regular local ring R of dimension ≥ 2, H^2_ét(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian, regular, of dimension d ≥ 2; U_R its punctured spectrum (PF.0).
proofSteps: U_R is a regular Noetherian integral scheme, so H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) is torsion (PF.5/gm-cohomology-torsion(b)).
d = 2: PF.5/regular-dimension-two-extension (Grothendieck, Brauer III 6.1 b)).

d ≥ 3: fix n ≥ 1. The Kummer sequence (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11) makes H^2(U_R, μ_n) → H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m)[n] surjective. In the support sequence H^2(R, μ_n) → H^2(U_R, μ_n) → H^3_𝔪(R, μ_n), the first group vanishes because R is strictly henselian (H^i_ét(R, 𝔾_m) = 0 for i ≥ 1, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.15, and Kummer), and the last vanishes by PF.4/flat-purity-regular (3 ≤ d). Hence H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m)[n] = 0 for every n, and H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0.

This is the route of CS24 Theorem 1.1.3(b); it covers C19's equal-characteristic, mixed-characteristic, prime-to-p and dimension-three cases at once. C19's own proof (passage to finite flat covers by Corollary 2.5, the towers of Lemmas 5.1–5.2, vanishing of the p-primary Brauer group of perfect schemes and of perfectoid rings, Gabber's dimension-three theorem and absolute purity) is an alternative whose inputs are routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations and PerfectoidQuotients Part II as sources.

sources.match: For strictly henselian regular local R of dimension ≥ 2, H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0; dimension 2 by Grothendieck, dimension 3 by Gabber, the prime-to-p part by absolute purity, and the remaining p-primary part by finite flat descent and perfectoid towers.

For R = W(k̄)⟦x, y, z⟧ (mixed characteristic, dimension 4) the p-primary part of H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) vanishes, the case left open before C19.

planet.name: Strict-local purity for the Brauer group

nodes.title: Tori on punctured spectra of henselian regular local rings with small residue fields
nodes.statement: For a henselian regular local ring R of dimension ≥ 2 whose residue field k has dimension ≤ 1 (H^i(k, G) = 0 for i ≥ 2 and every commutative finite étale G, and, if char k > 0, Br(k') = 0 for every finite separable k'/k), and an R-torus T, H^1_ét(U_R, T) = H^2_ét(U_R, T) = 0.
hypotheses: R henselian (not necessarily strictly), regular, dim ≥ 2; k of dimension ≤ 1 in Serre's sense (C19 Definition A.1); T an R-torus.
proofSteps: For finite étale local R'/R, pullback H^i(U_R, T) → H^i(U_{R'}, T) is injective for i = 1, 2 (C19 Corollary 2.4, from Propositions 2.2–2.3 on homogeneous spaces Res_{R'/R}(T_{R'})/T and Lemma A.2 for tori over fields of dimension ≤ 1; recorded gap SF-PII-tori, with the commutativity correction of C19 E1).
Passing to the colimit over all finite étale local R' (étale cohomology commutes with the limit, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.15) reduces to R strictly henselian, where T is split.
Then H^1(U_R, 𝔾_m) = Pic(U_R) = 0 (PF.5/local-picard-torsion-vanishing, regular case) and H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0 (PF.6/strict-local-brauer-purity).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.4, p. 3; §5.4, p. 13; Corollary 2.4, p. 5; Definition A.1 and Lemma A.2, p. 15
sources.match: For henselian regular R of dimension ≥ 2 with residue field of dimension ≤ 1 and an R-torus T, H^1 and H^2 of T on U_R vanish, by injectivity of pullback to finite étale covers and the strictly henselian case.

acceptance: For R strictly henselian and T = 𝔾_m it is Pic(U_R) = 0 and PF.6/strict-local-brauer-purity.
For R = ℤ_p⟦x⟧ (henselian, residue field 𝔽_p of dimension 1) and T = 𝔾_m: H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0.

The residue-field hypothesis cannot be dropped: for R = ℝ⟦x, y⟧ and T the norm-one torus of ℂ/ℝ, H^1(U_R, T) ≅ H^1(R, T) ≅ H^1(ℝ, T) = ℤ/2 by PF.6/torus-purity and henselian invariance, and ℝ does not have dimension ≤ 1.

nodes.title: The coniveau spectral sequence for cohomology with supports
nodes.statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension, Z ⊂ X closed and F an abelian sheaf on X_ét (for instance 𝔾_m). There is a convergent spectral sequence E_1^{a,b} = ⊕_{z ∈ Z, dim 𝒪_{X,z} = a} H^{a+b}_{z}(Spec 𝒪_{X,z}, F) ⇒ H^{a+b}_Z(X, F), where H_z denotes cohomology with supports in the closed point of Spec 𝒪_{X,z}; it arises from the filtration by families of closed supports contained in Z of codimension at least a in X.
hypotheses: X Noetherian of finite dimension; F an abelian étale sheaf. Any fppf analogue used here must include the continuity hypotheses of PF.0 for its local terms.
proofSteps: For each a use the filtered family Φ^a of closed W ⊂ Z all of whose points have codimension at least a in X. Take filtered colimits of the support triple sequences over W′ ⊂ W with W′ ∈ Φ^{a+1} and W ∈ Φ^a; exactness of filtered colimits gives the exact couple. The set of all points of codimension at least a need not be closed and is never used as a single closed support.

The graded pieces are computed by shrinking around the finitely many generic points of a closed support and then taking the colimit. Excision and localization give ⊕_{z∈Z, dim 𝒪_{X,z}=a} H^i_z(Spec 𝒪_{X,z},F). Each class occurs on a finite closed support, which explains the direct sum.

The bounded codimension range for finite-dimensional Noetherian X gives convergence. For fppf coefficients retain the same support formalism and the finite-presentation continuity hypotheses when identifying point terms by limits; the unrestricted étale assertion is the stated target.

sources.match: The coniveau spectral sequence with E_1 terms the cohomology with supports at the points of Z of given codimension reduces the vanishing of H^q_Z(X, 𝔾_m) to the case Z = closed point of a regular local X.

sources.locator: Exposé XVIII-A, §2.2, Lemma 2.2 and display (2.a), p. 333 in arXiv:1207.3648v1
sources.match: Directly read: families of closed supports indexed by codimension give the coniveau spectral sequence. The preprint numbering is Lemma 2.2/display (2.a), while C19 cites the published 2.2.1.
The coniveau spectral sequence for 𝔾_m (not read; cited through C19 p. 13).

acceptance: For Z = {x} a closed point it degenerates to H^i_Z(X, F) = H^i_x(Spec 𝒪_{X,x}, F) (excision).
For X a Dedekind scheme and Z = X it gives the localization sequence relating H^i(X, F), H^i(K, F) and ⊕_x H^{i+1}_x.
In C19 it is applied with F = 𝔾_m and X regular, strictly henselian of dimension ≥ 2.

nodes.title: Vanishing of torus cohomology with supports in degrees ≤ 3
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme, Z ⊂ X a closed subset with X ∖ Z → X quasi-compact, and T an X-torus. If 𝒪_{X,z} is regular of dimension ≥ 2 for every z ∈ Z, then H^q_Z(X, T) = 0 for q ≤ 3.
hypotheses: X arbitrary; T an X-torus (étale locally isomorphic to 𝔾_m^r); cohomology étale, equal to fppf (T smooth).
proofSteps: By the local-to-global spectral sequence (PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports) it suffices that the étale sheaves ℋ^q_Z(−, T) vanish for q ≤ 3. Tori are étale locally split, so T = 𝔾_m, and quasi-compactness of X ∖ Z → X identifies the stalk at x̄ with H^q_{Z ×_X Spec 𝒪^sh_{X,x̄}}(Spec 𝒪^sh_{X,x̄}, 𝔾_m) (limit argument, SGA 4 VII 5.9).

So assume X strictly henselian regular local of dimension ≥ 2 with Z ≠ ∅, hence Noetherian of finite dimension. The coniveau spectral sequence (PF.6/coniveau-spectral-sequence) reduces to Z the closed point of a regular local scheme of dimension ≥ 2, and the first step reduces again to X strictly local.

For X = Spec R strictly local regular of dimension ≥ 2 and Z the closed point: H^0(R, 𝔾_m) ≅ H^0(U_R, 𝔾_m) (depth ≥ 2, PF.0/hartogs-regular-sequence), H^i(R, 𝔾_m) = 0 for i > 0 (strictly henselian), H^1(U_R, 𝔾_m) = Pic(U_R) = 0 (PF.5/local-picard-torsion-vanishing) and H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0 (PF.6/strict-local-brauer-purity); the support sequence gives H^q_𝔪(R, 𝔾_m) = 0 for q ≤ 3.

sources.match: Reduction of H^q_Z(X, T) = 0 for q ≤ 3 to strictly henselian regular local rings of dimension ≥ 2 by the local-to-global spectral sequence, a limit argument and the coniveau spectral sequence, and the local vanishing from Hartogs, Pic(U_R) = 0 and Theorem 5.3.

acceptance: For X = Spec R with R strictly henselian regular of dimension 2 and Z the closed point it is equivalent to Pic(U_R) = 0 and H^2(U_R, 𝔾_m) = 0.
Codimension one is excluded: for Z = V(x) ⊂ 𝔸^2, H^1_Z(𝔸^2, 𝔾_m) ≅ ℤ (the divisor of x) ≠ 0.
Degree 4 is not covered: H^4_Z may be nonzero, which is why only injectivity on H^3 is asserted in PF.6/torus-purity.

nodes.title: Purity for tori along regular closed subsets of codimension ≥ 2
nodes.statement: For a scheme X, an X-torus T and a closed Z ⊂ X with X ∖ Z → X quasi-compact such that 𝒪_{X,z} is regular of dimension ≥ 2 for every z ∈ Z, restriction H^q_ét(X, T) → H^q_ét(X ∖ Z, T) is an isomorphism for q ≤ 2 and injective for q = 3.
hypotheses: As in PF.6/torus-low-support-vanishing.
proofSteps: The long exact sequence of PF.0/flat-cohomology-with-supports and PF.6/torus-low-support-vanishing (H^q_Z(X, T) = 0 for q ≤ 3).

sources.match: Bijectivity of restriction of torus cohomology in degrees ≤ 2 and injectivity in degree 3 across a closed subset along which the local rings are regular of dimension ≥ 2.

acceptance: For T = 𝔾_m and q = 1 it is Pic(X) ≅ Pic(X ∖ Z) for regular X and Z of codimension ≥ 2.
For X = 𝔸^2_ℂ and Z = {0}: Br(𝔸^2_ℂ ∖ {0}) = Br(𝔸^2_ℂ) = 0.
For d = 3 and regular local rings of dimension ≥ 2 it strengthens PF.5/multiplicative-type-purity-higher for tori.

nodes.title: Purity for the Brauer group of regular schemes
nodes.statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme X and a closed Z ⊂ X such that 𝒪_{X,z} is regular of dimension ≥ 2 for every z ∈ Z, restriction H^2_ét(X, 𝔾_m) → H^2_ét(X ∖ Z, 𝔾_m) is an isomorphism and H^3_ét(X, 𝔾_m) → H^3_ét(X ∖ Z, 𝔾_m) is injective.
hypotheses: X locally Noetherian, so X ∖ Z → X is quasi-compact; no regularity is assumed away from Z.
proofSteps: Apply PF.6/torus-purity with T = 𝔾_m.

sources.match: Bijectivity on H^2 and injectivity on H^3 of 𝔾_m-cohomology across a closed subset along which the local rings are regular of dimension ≥ 2, for locally Noetherian X: the purity conjecture of Grothendieck and Auslander–Goldman.

acceptance: For X regular and Z of codimension ≥ 2, Br′(X) ≅ Br′(X ∖ Z).
Codimension two is necessary: Br(𝔸^2_ℂ) = 0 while the complement of the coordinate axes has nonzero Brauer group (PF.6/codimension-one-deletion-example).
Regularity along Z is necessary: for the three-dimensional complete intersection of PF.5/brauer-purity-sharpness, Br(U_R) is infinite while Br(R) = 0.

nodes.title: Generic injectivity of H^2 for a torus
nodes.statement: Let X be a Noetherian integral regular scheme with function field K and T an X-torus. T has generically injective H^2 on X if for every nonempty open V ⊂ X the pullback H^2_ét(V, T) → H^2_ét(Spec K, T) is injective.
hypotheses: X Noetherian integral regular; T an X-torus.
proofSteps: A property of the pair (X, T); it is stable under passing to nonempty opens of X.

sources.match: The injectivity hypothesis on H^2 of every nonempty open into H^2 of the generic point, satisfied by 𝔾_m and by flasque tori and failing for some tori.

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.PurityForFlatCohomology.GenericallyInjectiveH2.flasque

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.PurityForFlatCohomology.GenericallyInjectiveH2.prod

examples (flasque tori) and counterexample (norm-one torus over ℙ^1_ℝ)

acceptance: Holds for 𝔾_m and flasque tori; fails for the norm-one torus over ℙ^1_ℝ.

nodes.title: H^2 of a torus as an intersection over codimension-one points
nodes.statement: Let X be a Noetherian integral regular scheme with function field K and T an X-torus with generically injective H^2 (PF.6/generic-h2-injectivity). Then H^2_ét(X, T) = ⋂_{x ∈ X^{(1)}} H^2_ét(Spec 𝒪_{X,x}, T) inside H^2_ét(K, T).
hypotheses: X Noetherian integral regular; x ranges over points of height one; the local groups embed in H^2(K, T) by the injectivity hypothesis applied to opens and a limit.
proofSteps: Let α lie in the intersection. If α extends to H^2(U, T) and to H^2(V, T) for nonempty opens U, V, then by the Mayer–Vietoris sequence for {U, V} (PF.0, API mayerVietoris) and injectivity of H^2(U ∩ V, T) → H^2(K, T), α extends to H^2(U ∪ V, T).

By a limit argument α extends over a neighbourhood of each height-one point, hence to an open U containing all height-one points; X ∖ U has codimension ≥ 2 with regular local rings, so PF.6/torus-purity extends α to H^2(X, T).

sources.match: Under generic injectivity, H^2(X, T) is the intersection of the H^2(𝒪_{X,x}, T) over height-one points, by Mayer–Vietoris glueing of extensions and Theorem 6.1.

acceptance: For X a Dedekind scheme the statement is the usual description of H^2(X, T) as classes unramified at every closed point.
Without generic injectivity it can fail: PF.6/norm-torus-counterexample gives a nonzero class on ℙ^1_ℝ that vanishes at the generic point.

nodes.title: The Auslander–Goldman question: the Brauer group as an intersection over codimension one
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian integral regular scheme X with function field K, H^2_ét(X, 𝔾_m) = ⋂_{x ∈ X^{(1)}} H^2_ét(𝒪_{X,x}, 𝔾_m) inside H^2_ét(K, 𝔾_m).
hypotheses: X Noetherian integral regular.
proofSteps: 𝔾_m has generically injective H^2 (PF.6/generic-h2-injectivity, API gm), so PF.6/codimension-one-torus-intersection applies.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.2 (= Theorem 6.2 for 𝔾_m), p. 2; Lemma 3.2, p. 7
sources.match: The Brauer group of a Noetherian integral regular scheme is the intersection of the Brauer groups of its local rings at height-one points inside the Brauer group of the function field, answering the question of Auslander and Goldman for affine X.

acceptance: For X = Spec R with R regular affine, this is the Auslander–Goldman description Br(R) = ⋂_{ht 𝔭 = 1} Br(R_𝔭) (Br = Br′ on affines by Gabber).
For X = 𝔸^2_ℂ: every class of Br(ℂ(x, y)) unramified along all curves is zero.

nodes.title: Flasque tori have generically injective H^2
nodes.statement: Let X be a Noetherian integral regular scheme and T an X-torus that is flasque: there is a finite étale Galois cover X'/X splitting T such that the Gal(X'/X)-module Hom_{X'-gp}(T_{X'}, 𝔾_{m,X'}) admits no nontrivial extension by any permutation module ℤ[Gal(X'/X)/H]. Then T has generically injective H^2 on X. Every torus direct factor of Res_{X''/X}(𝔾_m) for a finite étale X''/X is flasque.
hypotheses: X Noetherian integral regular; the flasque condition as in Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc 1987, 0.5 and 1.2; the scheme-level theory of tori and their character modules is recorded in the gap SF-PII-tori.
proofSteps: Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc 1987, Theorem 2.2(ii): for flasque T, H^2(V, T) → H^2(K, T) is injective on regular integral V; restrict to nonempty opens.
Direct factors of quasi-trivial tori Res_{X''/X}𝔾_m are flasque because permutation character modules have no nontrivial extensions by permutation modules (Shapiro's lemma and H^1(H, ℤ) = 0).

sources.match: Flasque tori, defined through Galois-module extensions of the character module by permutation modules, satisfy the injectivity hypothesis (6.2.1), e.g. torus direct factors of Weil restrictions of 𝔾_m along finite étale covers.

Directly read: flasqueness of a character lattice is equivalent to vanishing Ext¹ into every permutation lattice; flasque tori on integral geometrically locally factorial schemes have injective H² restriction to nonempty opens and the generic point.

acceptance: T = 𝔾_m and T = Res_{X'/X}𝔾_m are flasque.

For the norm-one torus of ℂ/ℝ, its character lattice ℤ_sign is not flasque: 0 → ℤ_trivial → ℤ[ℤ/2] → ℤ_sign → 0 is nonsplit, giving Ext¹(ℤ_sign,ℤ_trivial) = ℤ/2. The sublattice ℤ_trivial is a permutation lattice; using the regular permutation lattice as the Ext target would instead give zero.

nodes.title: Generic injectivity fails for the norm-one torus over ℙ^1_ℝ
nodes.statement: Let X = ℙ^1_ℝ and T the base change to X of the norm-one torus defined by 0 → T → Res_{ℂ/ℝ}(𝔾_m) → 𝔾_{m,ℝ} → 0 (the second map the norm). Then H^2_ét(X, T) contains a nonzero class whose restriction to the generic point vanishes.
hypotheses: X = ℙ^1_ℝ; T as displayed.
proofSteps: The norm map Res_{ℂ/ℝ}𝔾_m → 𝔾_m restricted to the open 𝔾_{m,ℝ} ⊂ ℙ^1_ℝ is a T-torsor over 𝔾_{m,ℝ} whose fibres over real points sweep out H^1(ℝ, T) ≅ ℤ/2, so it is not constant.
Every T-torsor over 𝔸^1_ℝ is constant (Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc 1987, 2.4).

Cover ℙ^1_ℝ by two copies of 𝔸^1 meeting in 𝔾_{m,ℝ}; the Mayer–Vietoris sequence (PF.0, API mayerVietoris) maps the non-constant torsor to a nonzero class in H^2(ℙ^1_ℝ, T), which is generically trivial because it is trivial on each 𝔸^1.

sources.match: The norm-one torus sequence over ℝ, viewed as a torsor over 𝔾_{m,ℝ}, is not constant while all torsors over 𝔸^1_ℝ are, so Mayer–Vietoris produces a nonzero generically trivial class in H^2(ℙ^1_ℝ, T).
Directly read: H¹(A,S) ≅ H¹(A[T_1,…,T_r],S) for a regular ring A and torus S, hence torsors on 𝔸¹ over a field are constant.

acceptance: The class restricts to zero in H^2(ℝ(t), T), so the intersection formula of PF.6/codimension-one-torus-intersection fails for this T.
H^1(ℝ, T) = ℝ^×/N(ℂ^×) = ℤ/2 is the source of the non-constancy.

nodes.title: The residue homomorphism of a discrete valuation ring on Brauer groups
nodes.statement: Let 𝒪 be a DVR with fraction field K and residue field k. Fix a prime ℓ different from char k, or ℓ = char k with k perfect. Pull back Br(K)[ℓ^∞] to Br(K̂)[ℓ^∞]. For the complete field K̂ and its maximal unramified extension K̂^unr, Br(K̂^unr)[ℓ^∞] = 0 gives the Hochschild–Serre identification with H²(G_k,(K̂^unr)^×)[ℓ^∞]. Apply the valuation, then the inverse of δ : H¹(k,ℚ/ℤ) ≅ H²(k,ℤ) from 0 → ℤ → ℚ → ℚ/ℤ → 0. The composite is the ℓ-primary residue ∂_𝒪. No isomorphism Br(K) ≅ Br(K̂) is assumed.
hypotheses: 𝒪 a DVR; ℓ as stated (for ℓ = char k with k imperfect no such exact residue theory exists, Poonen Warning 6.8.2).
The vanishing Br(K^unr)[ℓ^∞] = 0 for complete K with perfect residue field (Lang's theorem that K^unr is C_1; for ℓ ≠ char k, Grothendieck, Brauer III, 1.3) is recorded in the gap BR-RESIDUE-LANG.
proofSteps: Define the residue for a complete DVR using maximal-unramified Galois cohomology and the valuation; the permitted-primary vanishing over K̂^unr is exactly gap BR-RESIDUE-LANG.

For an arbitrary DVR, define ∂ by pullback to completion. Compatibility with henselization and unramified base change is part of the residue construction; it never requires a completion isomorphism on Brauer groups.

Use δ^{-1} after the valuation map. Fix the crossed-product convention by generators u a = σ(a)u and u^n = π for an unramified cyclic extension L/K of degree n, with χ(σ)=1/n. With this convention ∂[(L/K,σ,π)] = χ; this fixes the sign.

sources.match: For a discrete valuation ring, the residue sequence on ℓ-primary Brauer groups for ℓ ≠ char k, and for ℓ = char k when k is perfect (Grothendieck, Brauer III, 2.1).

sources.locator: Proposition 6.8.1 and the construction after it, pp. 196–197; Warning 6.8.2, p. 197
sources.match: The residue homomorphism Br K → H^1(k, ℚ/ℤ) through the maximal unramified extension and the valuation, with the caveat that p-primary parts are excluded when k is imperfect of characteristic p.

tests.statement: For 𝒪 = ℤ_p, ∂ : Br(ℚ_p) → H¹(𝔽_p,ℚ/ℤ) is an isomorphism. Evaluating its character on arithmetic Frobenius agrees with the local invariant normalized by the displayed crossed product; check the Frobenius convention when adapting Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory.

tests.name: TauCetiRoadmap.PurityForFlatCohomology.brauerResidue_laurent
tests.statement: For 𝒪 = ℂ⟦t⟧, H^1(ℂ, ℚ/ℤ) = 0 and Br(ℂ((t))) = 0, so ∂ = 0.

tests.name: TauCetiRoadmap.PurityForFlatCohomology.not_brauerResidue_imperfect
tests.statement: For 𝒪 = k⟦t⟧ with k separably closed and imperfect of characteristic p, Br(𝒪) = 0 and H^1(k, ℚ/ℤ) = 0 but Br(k((t)))[p] ≠ 0, so no exact p-primary residue sequence exists (Poonen Warning 6.8.2).

uses.how: the residue sequence for DVRs and its global form (6.4.4)
the global residue sequence on regular integral schemes

acceptance: For ℤ_p the residue is the local invariant Br(ℚ_p) ≅ ℚ/ℤ.
No exact p-primary residue exists over k⟦t⟧ with k separably closed imperfect.

nodes.title: The residue sequence of a discrete valuation ring
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of PF.6/brauer-residue, the sequence 0 → H^2_ét(𝒪, 𝔾_m)[ℓ^∞] → H^2_ét(K, 𝔾_m)[ℓ^∞] → H^1_ét(k, ℚ/ℤ)[ℓ^∞] is exact. No surjectivity of the residue is asserted.
hypotheses: As in PF.6/brauer-residue.
proofSteps: Injectivity: PF.5/gm-cohomology-torsion(b) for the regular one-dimensional Spec 𝒪.

For complete 𝒪, use 0 → (𝒪^unr)^× → (K^unr)^× → ℤ → 0, its Galois-cohomology sequence and the henselian Brauer identification Br(𝒪) ≅ Br(k). This identifies the kernel with the unramified classes in the admissible primary parts.

For an arbitrary DVR, use the unramified descent criterion: a class of Br(K)[ℓ^∞] whose pullback lies in Br(𝒪̂)[ℓ^∞] already extends over 𝒪. This is the remaining scheme-localization input in Poonen Proposition 6.8.1 (Grothendieck Brauer III, Proposition 2.1), recorded separately as gap BR-RESIDUE-DESCENT. Completion alone proves only the complete case.

nodes.title: The residue sequence of a regular integral scheme
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian integral regular scheme X with function field K, the sequence 0 → H^2_ét(X, 𝔾_m) → H^2_ét(K, 𝔾_m) → ⊕_{x ∈ X^{(1)}} H^1_ét(k(x), ℚ/ℤ) is exact after excluding the p-primary parts of all groups for every prime p such that some height-one point x has an imperfect residue field k(x) of characteristic p.
hypotheses: X Noetherian integral regular; for each excluded p the p-primary parts of all three groups are removed.
proofSteps: Combine PF.6/brauer-codimension-one-intersection (H^2(X, 𝔾_m) is the intersection of the H^2(𝒪_{X,x}, 𝔾_m) over height-one x) with PF.6/dvr-brauer-residue-sequence for each 𝒪_{X,x} (a DVR) in the admissible primary parts; the residue of a class is nonzero at only finitely many x (it extends over a dense open).

nodes.title: Points of height ≥ 2 in characteristic p force imperfect height-one residue fields
nodes.statement: Let X be a Noetherian integral regular scheme with a point y of height ≥ 2 and residue characteristic p > 0. Then y specializes from (is a specialization of) a point x of height one with residue characteristic p whose residue field k(x) carries a nontrivial discrete valuation; in particular k(x) is imperfect, so the p-primary parts are excluded in PF.6/global-brauer-residue-sequence.
hypotheses: X Noetherian integral regular; y of height ≥ 2 with char k(y) = p.
proofSteps: Choose a height-one prime of 𝒪_{X,y} containing p (or, in equal characteristic p, any height-one prime): it gives x with char k(x) = p. The closure of x is a scheme of dimension ≥ 1 at y, so k(x) is the function field of a Noetherian local domain of positive dimension and carries a nontrivial discrete valuation (EGA II 7.1.7).
A field of characteristic p with a nontrivial discrete valuation v is imperfect: a uniformizer has valuation 1, not divisible by p.

sources.match: A point of residue characteristic p and height ≥ 2 generalizes to a height-one point of residue characteristic p whose residue field has a nontrivial discrete valuation (EGA II 7.1.7), hence is imperfect, so the p-primary parts are excluded.

nodes.title: Removing a divisor changes the Brauer group
nodes.statement: The Brauer group of 𝔸^2_ℂ is zero, while the Brauer group of the complement of the two coordinate axes, 𝔾_m^2 over ℂ, is nonzero; hence the codimension ≥ 2 hypothesis of PF.6/brauer-purity-regular cannot be weakened to codimension 1.
hypotheses: Over ℂ; the coordinate axes form a divisor.
proofSteps: On 𝔾_m² over ℂ choose a primitive nth root ζ, n ≥ 2, and the cyclic algebra generated by v^n = y, u^n = x, u v = ζ v u. It is Azumaya where x and y are units. Along x = 0 it is the crossed product with unramified extension adjoining an nth root of y, σ(v)=ζv, so PF.6/brauer-residue gives the nonzero character of y in H¹(ℂ(y),ℤ/n). Thus its generic class and its class on 𝔾_m² are nonzero. Br(𝔸²_ℂ) = 0 is the homotopy-invariance calculation cited in C19 §1 through DeMeyer–Ford Remark 3.

acceptance: For the displayed crossed product, the x = 0 residue is the Kummer character of y, nonzero in ℂ(y)^×/ℂ(y)^{×n}. The explicit generators specify the convention instead of leaving the sign of a symbol (x,y)_n ambiguous.
